catalog.name: Purchasing calculations
catalog.description: Every formula, algorithm, rounding rule and worked example of the purchasing domain, in a structured form a rebuild can test against: the three named decimal precisions and the rounding vocabulary, the currency and unit conversions, the line and header amounts under each tax rounding method, the order currency rate, the approval threshold, the expected arrival of a line and of an order, the received quantity under each of its three methods, the billed quantity and the quantity to bill under each bill control policy, the at-date quantities and the amount still to bill, the gross unit price, the unit price handed to a goods movement, the preparation of a bill line, the four punctuality figures, the replenishment suggestion under each basis, the five grouping windows and the two order deadline rules, the lead-time contribution of a buy rule, the merge of two requests for quotation, the six parts of the bill matching routine, the price difference at billing time with its journal items, the five steps of valuing a goods movement from its bills, the eleven purchase analysis figures, the late search, the purchased quantity over the last year, the project profitability contribution, and the five parts of the accrued-expense computation.

records.name: The named decimal precisions of the purchasing domain
records.purpose: Fixes which named decimal precision governs each kind of purchasing figure, so that a rebuild rounds quantities, the unit price handed to a stock move and discount percentages exactly where the domain does.

operands.name: Product Unit decimal precision
operands.source: the named decimal precision record for product units, which an administrator may change
operands.constraints: shipped as 2 digits; a whole number of digits, never negative

operands.name: Product Price decimal precision
operands.source: the named decimal precision record for product prices, which an administrator may change
operands.constraints: shipped as 2 digits; a whole number of digits, never negative

operands.name: Discount decimal precision
operands.source: the named decimal precision record for discounts, which an administrator may change
operands.constraints: shipped as 2 digits; a whole number of digits, never negative

operands.name: quantity figure
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line, of the move or of the product
operands.source: the ordered quantity, the received quantity, the billed quantity or the quantity still to bill
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: unit price handed to a stock move
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of the product
operands.source: the computed valuation price of an incoming goods movement
operands.constraints: may be zero; negative only when the ordered quantity is negative

operands.name: discount percentage
operands.source: the discount typed on the order line
operands.constraints: from 0 to 100 in ordinary use; 100 is legal and yields a zero subtotal

preconditions.condition: The three named decimal precision records exist.
preconditions.otherwise: The shipped value of 2 digits applies to the missing one, because a named precision that cannot be read falls back to its shipped digit count.

procedure: Read the Product Unit decimal precision and use it for every quantity: ordered, received, billed and still to bill.
Read the Product Price decimal precision and use it both for the unit price handed to a goods movement and for the comparison that decides whether a price difference exists at billing time.
Read the Discount decimal precision and use it for the discount percentage of a line.
Round each figure half away from zero to its own precision at the moment the figure is written or compared, never earlier: intermediate arithmetic keeps full precision.

Keep the rounding of a currency separate from these three: a currency carries its own rounding step and its own number of decimal places, and money is rounded to that step and not to a named decimal precision.
records.formula: rounded_quantity = round_to_precision( quantity , Product Unit digits ) ; rounded_move_unit_price = round_to_precision( unit price handed to the move , Product Price digits ) ; rounded_discount = round_to_precision( discount percentage , Discount digits ) ; with Product Unit digits = 2 , Product Price digits = 2 and Discount digits = 2 as shipped

rounding.what: Quantities, the unit price handed to a goods movement, the price comparison at billing time, and the discount percentage.
rounding.precision: Product Unit for quantities, Product Price for the movement unit price and the price comparison, Discount for the discount percentage; 2 digits each as shipped.
rounding.step: At the moment the figure is written to its field or compared with another figure; intermediate arithmetic is not rounded.

result.name: rounded figure
result.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the quantity, the company currency for a price, or a percentage
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the field the figure belongs to, and used as the tolerance of the comparison it governs.

edge_cases.case: An administrator raises the Product Unit precision to 3 digits.
edge_cases.outcome: Every quantity comparison and every stored quantity immediately uses 3 digits; no stored value is rewritten, so a quantity written earlier keeps the value it was rounded to.

edge_cases.case: A quantity smaller in absolute value than half of one unit of the last digit.
edge_cases.outcome: It rounds to zero and every zero test at that precision reports it as zero, so the line is treated as having nothing to receive or nothing to bill.

edge_cases.case: A currency whose rounding step is coarser than the named precisions, for example a step of 1.
edge_cases.outcome: Money is rounded to the step of 1 while quantities keep 2 digits; the two roundings are independent and neither overrides the other.

worked_examples.description: The three precisions applied to one line at their shipped values
worked_examples.narrative: Each figure is rounded half away from zero to two digits: 7.005 becomes 7.01, 7.595 becomes 7.60 and 12.345 becomes 12.35. The three roundings are independent, and none of them is applied to the intermediate arithmetic that produced the figures.

records.name: Rounding an amount to the currency
records.purpose: Defines the single money-rounding operation used everywhere in the domain, so that every monetary figure a rebuild writes lands on a multiple of the currency's own rounding step.

operands.name: amount to round
operands.source: any monetary intermediate result: a subtotal, a tax amount, a total, an accrued amount
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: rounding step of the currency
operands.source: the currency record
operands.constraints: 0.01 for most currencies; strictly positive

preconditions.condition: The currency of the amount is known.
preconditions.otherwise: No monetary figure can be written and the calculation that needed it is not meaningful.

procedure: Divide the absolute value of the amount by the rounding step of the currency.
Round that ratio to the nearest whole number, resolving a tie of exactly one half away from zero.
Multiply the whole number back by the rounding step.
Restore the sign of the original amount.
records.formula: round_to_currency( amount ) = sign( amount ) × round_half_away_from_zero( | amount | ÷ rounding_step ) × rounding_step

rounding.what: The monetary amount handed in.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the currency, 0.01 for most currencies.
rounding.step: At the moment the amount is written to a monetary field, and at each step a formula names it explicitly.

result.name: rounded amount
result.unit_or_currency: the currency handed in
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the monetary field being written, or returned to the formula that asked for the rounding.

edge_cases.case: The amount is exactly on a half step, for example 19.595 with a step of 0.01.
edge_cases.outcome: It rounds away from zero, giving 19.60 for a positive amount and −19.60 for a negative one; the method is never half to even.

edge_cases.case: The amount is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The result is zero and the sign is positive.

edge_cases.case: The currency has a rounding step of 1.
edge_cases.outcome: Every amount lands on a whole number of currency units; no decimal is ever stored.

edge_cases.case: A formula asks for a conversion without rounding.
edge_cases.outcome: This operation is not applied at all; the unrounded figure is carried forward and rounded only once, later, by the caller that writes it.

worked_examples.description: Rounding a tax amount with the ordinary step of one hundredth
worked_examples.narrative: The absolute value divided by the step is 1959.51, which rounds to 1960, and multiplied back by 0.01 gives 19.60.

worked_examples.description: Rounding a negative amount that sits exactly on a half step
worked_examples.narrative: The absolute value divided by the step is 0.5, the tie is resolved away from zero to 1, and the sign is restored, giving minus 0.01.

records.name: Rounding to a named decimal precision
records.purpose: Defines the rounding of a non-monetary figure to a fixed number of decimal digits, which is how quantities, the movement unit price and several reported figures are fixed.

operands.name: value to round
operands.source: the figure being written or compared
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: number of decimal digits
operands.source: a named decimal precision, or a digit count written into the formula that asks for the rounding
operands.constraints: a whole number, never negative

preconditions.condition: The number of decimal digits is known.
preconditions.otherwise: The named precision falls back to its shipped digit count of 2.

procedure: Multiply the absolute value by ten raised to the number of decimal digits.
Round that product to the nearest whole number, resolving a tie of exactly one half away from zero.
Divide back by ten raised to the number of decimal digits.
Restore the sign of the original value.
records.formula: round_to_precision( value , digits ) = sign( value ) × round_half_away_from_zero( | value | × 10^digits ) ÷ 10^digits

rounding.what: The value handed in.
rounding.precision: The number of decimal digits handed in, most often a named decimal precision of 2 digits.
rounding.step: At the step the formula that calls it names; never applied to an intermediate result unless the formula says so.

result.name: rounded value
result.unit_or_currency: the unit, currency or percentage of the value handed in
result.stored_or_displayed: Returned to the caller, which stores it or compares it.

edge_cases.case: The digit count is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The value is rounded to a whole number, still half away from zero; this is what the dashboard on-time figure uses.

edge_cases.case: The value is exactly on a half at the last digit.
edge_cases.outcome: It rounds away from zero, so 2.345 at 2 digits becomes 2.35 and minus 2.345 becomes minus 2.35.

edge_cases.case: The value is already shorter than the digit count.
edge_cases.outcome: It is returned unchanged.

worked_examples.description: Rounding the average days to order to two digits
worked_examples.narrative: The value multiplied by one hundred is 249.99, which rounds to 250, and divided back by one hundred gives 2.50.

worked_examples.description: Rounding an on-time percentage to a whole number
worked_examples.narrative: With zero digits the value rounds to the nearest whole number, and 85.714… rounds to 86.

records.name: Rounding up to a number of decimal digits
records.purpose: Defines the away-from-zero rounding used by the replenishment suggestion, so that a suggested quantity is never short of the computed need.

operands.name: value to round
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the raw replenishment need
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: number of decimal digits
operands.source: the formula that asks for the rounding; the replenishment suggestion asks for 0
operands.constraints: a whole number, never negative

preconditions.condition: The value is a finite number.
preconditions.otherwise: The rounding is not attempted and the caller treats the need as zero.

procedure: Multiply the absolute value by ten raised to the number of decimal digits.
Take the smallest whole number that is not below that product, so that any fractional part at all pushes the result up.
Divide back by ten raised to the number of decimal digits.
Restore the sign of the original value, so that a negative value is rounded away from zero as well and never towards it.
records.formula: round_up( value , digits ) = sign( value ) × ceiling( | value | × 10^digits ) ÷ 10^digits

rounding.what: The value handed in, most often a suggested replenishment quantity.
rounding.precision: The number of decimal digits handed in; the replenishment suggestion uses 0 digits, that is whole units.
rounding.step: Once, on the raw need, before the maximum against zero is taken.

result.name: rounded value
result.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: Returned to the caller; the replenishment suggestion stores it as the suggested quantity.

edge_cases.case: The value has no fractional part.
edge_cases.outcome: It is returned unchanged; rounding up never adds a whole unit to an already whole value.

edge_cases.case: The value is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The magnitude is rounded up and the sign restored, so minus 5.108 at 0 digits becomes minus 6; the replenishment suggestion then clamps the result to zero.

edge_cases.case: The value is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The result is zero.

worked_examples.description: Rounding a raw replenishment need to whole units
worked_examples.narrative: The magnitude 24.784 has a fractional part, so the smallest whole number not below it is 25, and the suggestion is 25 units.

worked_examples.description: Rounding a raw need that is already whole
worked_examples.narrative: There is no fractional part, so the value is returned as 12 and no extra unit is added.

records.name: The zero test at a precision
records.purpose: Defines the only way the domain asks whether a quantity or an amount is zero, so that no rebuild compares a computed figure with zero exactly.

operands.name: value to test
operands.source: a quantity still to bill, a quantity to push to a goods movement, a price difference subtotal, an accrued amount
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: number of decimal digits
operands.source: the named decimal precision or the rounding of the unit of measure that governs the comparison
operands.constraints: a whole number, never negative

preconditions.condition: The precision that governs this comparison is the one named for it in the table of numeric comparison rules.
preconditions.otherwise: A comparison made at a different precision may report a different answer, and the two implementations then diverge on whether a line has anything left to bill.

procedure: Take the absolute value of the figure.
Compare it with one half of ten raised to minus the number of decimal digits.
Report the figure as zero when the absolute value is smaller than that bound, which is exactly the condition under which the figure would round to zero at that precision.
records.formula: is_zero_at_precision( value , digits ) = true when | value | < 0.5 × 10^(−digits) , false otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing is written; the operation only reports whether the figure would round to zero.
rounding.precision: The named decimal precision or the rounding of the unit of measure that governs the comparison, 2 digits in the ordinary case.
rounding.method: The bound is half of the last digit, which is the same threshold the half-away-from-zero rounding uses.
rounding.step: At every comparison with zero; the value itself is left unrounded.

result.name: verdict that the figure is zero
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, the result is a yes or no answer
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the branch that decided to ask.

edge_cases.case: The value is exactly one half of the last digit, for example 0.005 at 2 digits.
edge_cases.outcome: The strict comparison reports it as not zero, because the test is strictly smaller than the bound; the same value would round away from zero to 0.01.

edge_cases.case: The digit count is 0.
edge_cases.outcome: Any magnitude below one half is reported as zero.

edge_cases.case: The value is a negative figure of small magnitude.
edge_cases.outcome: The absolute value is used, so a small negative figure is reported as zero exactly like the matching positive one.

worked_examples.description: Testing a residual quantity still to bill at two digits
worked_examples.narrative: One half of ten to the power minus two is 0.005, and 0.004 is strictly below it, so the residual counts as zero and the line has nothing left to bill.

worked_examples.description: Testing a residual that sits exactly on the bound
worked_examples.narrative: The comparison is strict, so 0.005 is not below 0.005 and the residual counts as non-zero; the line still has something to bill.

records.name: The comparison at a precision
records.purpose: Defines the three-way comparison of two figures at a precision, which is how the domain decides that an ordered quantity has changed, that a received quantity has fallen short, or that a stored and a computed unit price still agree.

operands.name: first value
operands.source: the stored figure, or the left side of the comparison
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: second value
operands.unit_or_currency: the same unit or currency as the first
operands.source: the computed figure, or the right side of the comparison
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: number of decimal digits
operands.source: the named decimal precision or the rounding of the unit of measure that governs the comparison
operands.constraints: a whole number, never negative

preconditions.condition: The two values are expressed in the same unit or the same currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The comparison is meaningless; the values must first be converted, and the domain converts a quantity into the line unit and an amount into one currency before comparing.

procedure: Round the first value to the number of decimal digits, half away from zero.
Round the second value the same way.
Return minus one when the first rounded value is below the second, zero when they are equal, and one when the first is above the second.
records.formula: compare_at_precision( a , b , digits ) = −1 when round_to_precision( a , digits ) < round_to_precision( b , digits ) ; = 0 when they are equal ; = +1 when round_to_precision( a , digits ) > round_to_precision( b , digits )

rounding.what: Both values, before they are compared.
rounding.precision: The named decimal precision or the rounding of the unit of measure named for that comparison in the table of numeric comparison rules.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied to both sides.
rounding.step: Immediately before the comparison; neither value is written back rounded.

result.name: comparison verdict
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, the result is minus one, zero or one
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the branch that decided to ask.

edge_cases.case: Two values that differ only below the last digit.
edge_cases.outcome: They compare equal, so the domain treats the ordered quantity as unchanged and does not rewrite the goods movement.

edge_cases.case: The stored and the computed unit price of a bill line differ at the Product Price precision.
edge_cases.outcome: The price-difference adjustment at billing time is suppressed, which is exactly what happens when a discount has been applied.

edge_cases.case: One side is missing.
edge_cases.outcome: It is treated as zero and the comparison proceeds, so a missing computed price compares as zero against a stored price.

worked_examples.description: Deciding whether an ordered quantity has changed
worked_examples.narrative: Both values round to 10.00 at two digits, so the comparison returns zero and the ordered quantity counts as unchanged.

worked_examples.description: Deciding whether a stored unit price still equals the computed one
worked_examples.narrative: The stored price rounds to 10.00 and the computed price to 9.50, so the comparison returns one, the prices do not agree, and the price-difference adjustment is suppressed.

records.name: The precision used by each numeric comparison of the domain
records.purpose: Names, comparison by comparison, which precision the domain compares at, so that a rebuild reproduces each decision boundary rather than choosing one precision for everything.

operands.name: quantity still to bill
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the computed quantity to bill of a line
operands.constraints: compared with zero at the Product Unit precision

operands.name: ordered quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the total quantity of the line, before and after a change
operands.constraints: compared with its previous value at the Product Unit precision, and with the received or billed quantity at the rounding of the line unit

operands.name: quantity to push to a goods movement
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the difference between the ordered quantity and what has already been pushed
operands.constraints: compared with zero at the rounding of the line unit

operands.name: goods movement quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the movement
operands.source: the quantity of a stock movement
operands.constraints: compared with zero at the rounding of the movement unit to decide whether it is negative

operands.name: total of a generated document
operands.source: the total of a prepared vendor bill or refund
operands.constraints: compared with zero at the rounding of the document currency to decide whether the document type must be switched

operands.name: stored and computed unit prices
operands.source: the unit price stored on a bill line and the one recomputed for it
operands.constraints: compared at the Product Price precision

operands.name: component cost share
operands.source: the cost share of a kit component
operands.constraints: compared with zero, and the set totalled against 100, at two digits

operands.name: bill total against order total
operands.source: the total of an incoming bill and the sum of the remaining amounts of order lines
operands.constraints: compared with an absolute tolerance of 0.02

operands.name: two expected arrivals
operands.source: the expected arrival timestamps of two order lines that might merge
operands.constraints: compared with an absolute tolerance of 86 400 seconds

operands.name: bill line unit price against order line unit price
operands.source: the unit price of a bill line and of a candidate order line
operands.constraints: compared for exact equality, with no tolerance at all

preconditions.condition: The comparison being made is one of those named above.
preconditions.otherwise: No tolerance is assumed: the domain never compares two computed figures with an exact test unless the table says so, and the pairing of unit prices is the single exact test.

procedure: Identify which of the named comparisons is being made.
Take the precision or the tolerance named for it: a named decimal precision, the rounding of a unit of measure, the rounding of a currency, or an absolute tolerance.
Round both sides to that precision, or apply that absolute tolerance, and only then compare.
Never compare two computed figures without rounding first, except for the one pairing test that requires exact equality of unit prices.
records.formula: quantity to bill is zero → Product Unit ; ordered quantity changed → Product Unit ; ordered quantity decreased → rounding of the line unit ; quantity to push is zero → rounding of the line unit ; movement quantity is negative → rounding of the movement unit ; ordered quantity below billed quantity → rounding of the line unit ; generated document total is negative → rounding of the document currency ; stored unit price equals computed unit price → Product Price ; component cost share is zero and the set totals 100 → 2 digits ; bill total matches order total → absolute tolerance 0.02 in the bill currency ; two expected arrivals allow a merge → absolute tolerance 86 400 seconds ; bill line unit price equals order line unit price → exact equality

rounding.what: Both sides of every comparison listed.
rounding.precision: As named per comparison: Product Unit, Product Price, the rounding of a unit of measure, the rounding of a currency, two digits, or an absolute tolerance of 0.02 or 86 400 seconds.
rounding.method: Half away from zero where a precision is named; an absolute band where a tolerance is named; no rounding at all for the one exact-equality test.
rounding.step: Immediately before the comparison.

result.name: comparison verdict
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, the result is a yes or no answer or a three-way verdict
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; each verdict drives the branch that asked for it.

edge_cases.case: A quantity compared at the Product Unit precision but stored in a unit whose own rounding is coarser.
edge_cases.outcome: The two precisions can disagree; the domain uses the one named for that comparison and no other, which is why the table distinguishes them.

edge_cases.case: A bill total that differs from the order total by exactly 0.02.
edge_cases.outcome: The band is strict on both sides, so a difference of exactly the tolerance does not match; only a difference strictly below 0.02 matches.

edge_cases.case: Two expected arrivals exactly 86 400 seconds apart.
edge_cases.outcome: The merge test accepts it, because that comparison is stated as not exceeding 86 400 seconds.

worked_examples.description: The same pair of figures judged at two different precisions
worked_examples.narrative: At the Product Unit precision of two digits both figures round to 10.00 and count as equal, so the ordered quantity counts as unchanged; at the line unit's own rounding of 0.001 they are 10.004 and 10.000 and do not count as equal, so a test that uses the line unit rounding sees a decrease.

records.name: Converting a quantity and a price between units of measure
records.purpose: States how purchasing restates a quantity or a price from one unit of measure into another, which every received, billed and analysed quantity depends on.

operands.name: quantity or price to convert
operands.unit_or_currency: the source unit of measure, or a currency per source unit for a price
operands.source: a goods movement quantity, a bill line quantity, an order line quantity, or a unit price
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: source unit of measure
operands.source: the unit stored on the record holding the figure
operands.constraints: must belong to the same category as the target unit

operands.name: target unit of measure
operands.source: the unit of the line, or the reference unit of the product
operands.constraints: must belong to the same category as the source unit

operands.name: factor of each unit relative to the reference unit of its category
operands.source: the unit of measure record
operands.constraints: strictly positive; the factor of a unit is the number of reference units it contains, so a box of twelve pieces has a factor of twelve when the reference unit is the piece

operands.name: rounding of the target unit
operands.source: the unit of measure record
operands.constraints: strictly positive; the shipped value for a unit counted in whole pieces is 1

preconditions.condition: The two units belong to the same category.
preconditions.otherwise: The conversion is refused and the calling computation cannot proceed; a rebuild must treat a cross-category conversion as an error rather than as a factor of one.

preconditions.condition: The figure being converted is a quantity, not a price.
preconditions.otherwise: A price is converted with the inverse relation, because a price is an amount per unit: a quantity multiplied by a factor corresponds to a price divided by the same factor.

procedure: For a quantity, multiply by the factor of the source unit and divide by the factor of the target unit, both factors taken relative to the reference unit of the category.
Round the converted quantity to the rounding of the target unit, unless the caller names a different rounding method; the received-quantity computation names half away from zero explicitly.
For a price, multiply by the factor of the target unit and divide by the factor of the source unit, which is the inverse of the quantity relation.
Leave a converted price unrounded unless the caller that receives it rounds it, so that a chain of restatements does not accumulate rounding error.
records.formula: convert_quantity( q , from_unit , to_unit ) = q × ( factor(from_unit) ÷ factor(to_unit) ) , rounded to the rounding of to_unit unless another method is named ; convert_price( p , from_unit , to_unit ) = p × ( factor(to_unit) ÷ factor(from_unit) ) , unrounded

rounding.what: The converted quantity; a converted price is not rounded here.
rounding.precision: The rounding of the target unit of measure, or the method the caller names, which for the received quantity is half away from zero.
rounding.method: Half away from zero when named; otherwise the rounding of the target unit.
rounding.step: Immediately after the conversion of a quantity, and never on a converted price.

result.name: converted quantity or converted price
result.unit_or_currency: the target unit of measure, or a currency per target unit
result.stored_or_displayed: Returned to the caller; a converted quantity is stored on the received, billed or analysed quantity field, and a converted price is carried into the next step of a price computation.

edge_cases.case: The two units are the same.
edge_cases.outcome: The factors cancel and the figure is returned unchanged, with no rounding error introduced.

edge_cases.case: The target unit is coarser than the source unit, for example units into boxes.
edge_cases.outcome: The converted quantity acquires a fractional part; rounding it to the target unit's rounding can lose part of a box, which is why the received-quantity computation names the rounding method explicitly.

edge_cases.case: The quantity is negative, for example a return.
edge_cases.outcome: The sign is preserved and the half-away-from-zero rounding moves the magnitude away from zero.

worked_examples.description: Restating a movement quantity in units into the line's boxes
worked_examples.narrative: Seventy-two units divided by twelve units to the box gives six boxes exactly.

worked_examples.description: Restating a price per box into a price per unit
worked_examples.narrative: A price of 114.00 for a box that holds twelve units is 114.00 divided by twelve, that is 9.50 per unit; the converted price is left unrounded at this stage.

records.name: Converting an amount between currencies
records.purpose: States the single currency conversion purchasing performs, and names the two callers that ask for it without rounding, so that a rebuild rounds an amount exactly once on its way through a chain of conversions.

operands.name: amount to convert
operands.source: a line subtotal, an order total, an approval threshold, a bill line unit price or a valuation price
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero

operands.name: source currency
operands.source: the currency of the record holding the amount
operands.constraints: must exist

operands.name: target currency
operands.source: the currency the caller needs the amount in
operands.constraints: must exist

operands.name: company
operands.source: the company whose rate table is consulted, which is the order's company
operands.constraints: must exist

operands.name: date
operands.source: the conversion date the caller supplies, failing that the order deadline, failing that today
operands.constraints: must be a date, not a timestamp; a timestamp is reduced to its date part

operands.name: rate of a currency for that company on that date
operands.source: the rate table of the company
operands.constraints: strictly positive

preconditions.condition: A rate exists for both currencies for that company on or before that date.
preconditions.otherwise: The rate lookup falls back to the nearest earlier rate, and, when no earlier rate exists, to a rate of one, so the amount passes through unchanged.

preconditions.condition: The caller has said whether the result is to be rounded.
preconditions.otherwise: The result is rounded to the target currency, which is the default; the callers that need an unrounded figure say so explicitly.

procedure: Look up the rate of the target currency for the company on the date.
Look up the rate of the source currency for the company on the same date.
Multiply the amount by the first rate divided by the second.
Round the product to the target currency, unless the caller asked for no rounding, in which case carry the full precision forward.
records.formula: converted_amount = round_to_currency( amount × ( rate( to_currency , company , date ) ÷ rate( from_currency , company , date ) ) ) , and the same product left unrounded when the caller asks for no rounding

rounding.what: The converted amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the target currency.
rounding.step: Once, at the end of the conversion, and skipped entirely for the callers that ask for no rounding: the unit price of a prepared bill line, the company-currency balance of a prepared bill line, the value handed to a goods movement, and the valuation price used by the price-difference test.

result.name: converted amount
result.unit_or_currency: the target currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Returned to the caller; stored on the monetary field the caller is writing, or carried forward unrounded into the next step.

edge_cases.case: The two currencies are the same.
edge_cases.outcome: The two rates are equal, the ratio is one, and the amount is returned unchanged apart from the rounding.

edge_cases.case: The date is a timestamp.
edge_cases.outcome: Only its date part is used, so two conversions on the same day at different times use the same rate.

edge_cases.case: No rate exists at all for one of the currencies.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate falls back to one, and the amount passes through unchanged; a rebuild must not treat a missing rate as an error that blocks the purchase.

edge_cases.case: The caller asks for no rounding and then rounds later.
edge_cases.outcome: The intermediate figure keeps full precision, and the single rounding at the end can differ in the last digit from rounding at both steps; this is the reason the domain names the unrounded callers explicitly.

worked_examples.description: Converting an order subtotal into the company currency at a rate of one and a quarter
worked_examples.narrative: The amount is multiplied by one divided by 1.25, that is 0.8, giving 4 400.00, which is already on the currency step and is stored as 4 400.00.

records.name: The base line handed to the tax engine
records.purpose: Fixes exactly what purchasing hands the tax engine for each order line, because the engine's answer is what becomes the line's subtotal, tax and total.

operands.name: ordered quantity of the line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the total quantity field of the order line
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative; a display line is not handed over at all

operands.name: unit price of the line
operands.unit_or_currency: the order currency per line unit
operands.source: the unit price field of the order line
operands.constraints: may be zero; may be negative

operands.name: discount percentage of the line
operands.source: the discount field of the order line
operands.constraints: from 0 to 100 in ordinary use

operands.name: taxes of the line
operands.source: the tax set of the order line
operands.constraints: may be empty

operands.name: vendor of the order
operands.source: the partner of the order
operands.constraints: must be set; used by the engine for fiscal treatment

operands.name: currency of the order
operands.source: the currency of the order, or the company currency when the order carries none
operands.constraints: must exist

operands.name: rate of the order
operands.source: the stored currency rate of the order
operands.constraints: strictly positive

operands.name: description of the line
operands.source: the description field of the order line
operands.constraints: used as the label of the base line

preconditions.condition: The line is not a display line.
preconditions.otherwise: The line is skipped altogether and contributes nothing to any header amount.

preconditions.condition: The order carries a currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The company currency is used in its place, so the base line always has a currency.

procedure: Walk the order lines in their stored sequence and skip every display line.
For each remaining line, build one base line carrying the ordered quantity, the unit price, the discount percentage, the tax set, the vendor, the currency, the rate and the description.
Hand the whole set of base lines to the tax engine in one call, so that a company using global tax rounding can round the document's tax once instead of line by line.
Take the engine's per-line and document answers back and store them on the lines and on the header.
records.formula: base_line = ( quantity = ordered quantity , unit price = unit price of the line , discount percentage = discount of the line , taxes = taxes of the line , partner = vendor of the order , currency = order currency or company currency , rate = order currency rate , label = description of the line )

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded while the base line is built.
rounding.precision: Not applicable at this step; the rounding is the tax engine's, governed by the company's tax rounding method.
rounding.step: The whole set of base lines is handed over before any rounding happens, which is what makes global rounding possible.

result.name: set of base lines of the order
result.unit_or_currency: quantities in the line units and amounts in the order currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; handed to the tax engine, whose answers are stored on the lines and on the header.

edge_cases.case: The order has only display lines.
edge_cases.outcome: No base line is built, the engine is given an empty set, and every header amount is zero.

edge_cases.case: A line has a zero ordered quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: It is still handed over as a base line and contributes a subtotal of zero, so it still appears on a generated bill with quantity zero.

edge_cases.case: A line has a negative ordered quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: It is handed over unchanged and the arithmetic follows the sign, so the document total can become negative and the generated document becomes a vendor refund.

edge_cases.case: The order has no currency at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The company currency is substituted, so the engine is never given a base line without a currency.

worked_examples.description: Two ordinary lines and one section line handed over
worked_examples.narrative: The section line is skipped, so exactly two base lines are handed to the engine, each carrying its own quantity, unit price, discount and tax, together with the order's vendor, currency and rate.

records.name: The untaxed base of an order line
records.purpose: Gives the amount on which the taxes of a line are computed, before any rounding, which is the starting figure of every line amount and of the whole document total.

operands.name: ordered quantity of the line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the total quantity field of the order line
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: unit price of the line
operands.unit_or_currency: the order currency per line unit
operands.source: the unit price field of the order line
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: discount percentage of the line
operands.source: the discount field of the order line
operands.constraints: from 0 to 100 in ordinary use; 100 yields a base of zero

preconditions.condition: The line is not a display line.
preconditions.otherwise: No base is computed and the line contributes nothing.

procedure: Divide the discount percentage by one hundred and subtract the result from one, giving the retained fraction of the price.
Multiply the unit price by that retained fraction.
Multiply the result by the ordered quantity.
Leave the product unrounded: the rounding belongs to the tax engine and happens once, either per line or for the whole document, according to the company's tax rounding method.
records.formula: line_base = quantity × unit_price × ( 1 − discount_percentage ÷ 100 )

rounding.what: Nothing at this step; the base is carried at full precision into the tax computation.
rounding.precision: Not applicable at this step.
rounding.step: The base is rounded only when the tax engine writes the line subtotal, under per-line rounding, or when it writes the document total, under global rounding.

result.name: untaxed base of the line
result.unit_or_currency: the order currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored on its own; it becomes the line subtotal after the tax engine's rounding.

edge_cases.case: The discount is 100.
edge_cases.outcome: The retained fraction is zero and the base is zero, which is legal; the line contributes nothing to the totals.

edge_cases.case: The unit price is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The base is zero; the receipt movement is valued at zero and the whole standard cost becomes a price difference at billing time.

edge_cases.case: The ordered quantity is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The base is zero, and the line still appears on a generated bill with quantity zero.

edge_cases.case: The ordered quantity is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The base is negative and the arithmetic follows the sign, producing a refund.

worked_examples.description: A line of three units at 49.99 with a ten per cent discount
worked_examples.narrative: One minus ten divided by one hundred is 0.9, the discounted unit price is 44.991, and three of them give a base of 134.973, which is carried unrounded into the tax computation.

records.name: Line subtotal, line total and line tax amount
records.purpose: Gives the three monetary figures a purchase order line stores, all of them in the order currency, so that a rebuild stores the same three numbers and derives the tax as a difference rather than as a separate rounding.

operands.name: total excluding tax returned by the engine for the line
operands.source: the tax engine, given the line's base line
operands.constraints: already rounded by the engine according to the company's tax rounding method

operands.name: total including tax returned by the engine for the line
operands.source: the tax engine, given the line's base line
operands.constraints: already rounded by the engine

preconditions.condition: The line was handed to the tax engine as a base line.
preconditions.otherwise: It is a display line and stores no amounts at all; its subtotal, total and tax are zero.

procedure: Take the engine's total excluding tax for the line and store it as the line subtotal.
Take the engine's total including tax for the line and store it as the line total.
Subtract the subtotal from the total to obtain the tax amount of the line, rather than asking the engine for a separately rounded tax figure.
Store all three in the order currency.
records.formula: price_subtotal = total_excluded_in_order_currency ; price_total = total_included_in_order_currency ; price_tax = price_total − price_subtotal

rounding.what: The subtotal and the total, both rounded by the tax engine before purchasing stores them; the tax amount is not rounded again.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the order currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied by the tax engine.
rounding.step: The engine rounds before returning the two totals; purchasing then subtracts, so the tax amount inherits the rounding of the two figures and never introduces a third.

result.name: line subtotal, line total and line tax amount
result.unit_or_currency: the order currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the three amount fields of the purchase order line and shown on the order form.

edge_cases.case: The line carries no tax.
edge_cases.outcome: The total equals the subtotal and the tax amount is exactly zero.

edge_cases.case: The company uses global tax rounding.
edge_cases.outcome: The engine may return line figures whose sum differs in the last digit from a line-by-line rounding; the line still stores what the engine returned.

edge_cases.case: The line is a display line.
edge_cases.outcome: All three amounts are zero and the line is not handed to the engine at all.

edge_cases.case: The subtotal is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The total and the tax follow the sign, and the generated document becomes a vendor refund.

worked_examples.description: A line of seven units at 13.33 with a twenty-one per cent tax that is not included in the price
worked_examples.narrative: The subtotal is 93.31 and the total 112.91; the tax amount is the difference, 19.60, and is not rounded a second time.

records.name: The four header amounts of an order
records.purpose: Gives the four totals a purchase order stores, three in the order currency and one in the company currency, all taken from the tax engine over the whole set of base lines at once.

operands.name: base amount returned by the engine for the document
operands.source: the tax engine, given every non-display line at once
operands.constraints: already rounded by the engine

operands.name: tax amount returned by the engine for the document
operands.source: the tax engine
operands.constraints: already rounded by the engine

operands.name: total amount returned by the engine for the document
operands.source: the tax engine
operands.constraints: already rounded by the engine

operands.name: total amount in the company currency returned by the engine
operands.source: the tax engine
operands.constraints: derived by the engine, not by dividing the order total by the order rate

preconditions.condition: Every non-display line has been handed to the engine in one call.
preconditions.otherwise: A company using global tax rounding would round line by line instead and the document tax could differ in the last digit.

preconditions.condition: The order has a currency and a company.
preconditions.otherwise: The company currency is substituted for a missing order currency, and the company-currency total cannot be produced without a company.

procedure: Hand the whole set of base lines to the tax engine in a single call.
Store the engine's base amount as the untaxed total of the order.
Store the engine's tax amount as the tax total of the order.
Store the engine's total amount as the total of the order.
Store the engine's company-currency total as the order's total in the company currency, taking it from the engine rather than dividing the order total by the order rate.
records.formula: amount_untaxed = base_amount_in_order_currency ; amount_tax = tax_amount_in_order_currency ; amount_total = total_amount_in_order_currency ; amount_total_in_company_currency = total_amount_in_company_currency

rounding.what: The four header amounts, all rounded by the tax engine before purchasing stores them.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the order currency for the first three, and of the company currency for the fourth.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied by the tax engine.
rounding.step: Once, inside the engine, over the whole set of base lines; purchasing performs no further rounding on the header.

result.name: untaxed total, tax total, total and company-currency total of the order
result.unit_or_currency: the order currency for the first three, the company currency for the fourth
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the four amount fields of the purchase order, shown on the order form and used by the approval test.

edge_cases.case: The order has no line at all, or only display lines.
edge_cases.outcome: The engine is given an empty set and all four amounts are zero.

edge_cases.case: The order currency equals the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The fourth amount equals the third.

edge_cases.case: The order total is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The approval test still compares it with the threshold, and a generated bill is switched to a vendor refund after creation.

edge_cases.case: The company uses global tax rounding.
edge_cases.outcome: The document tax is rounded once for the whole document, so the sum of the line tax amounts may differ from the header tax amount in the last digit.

worked_examples.description: The header of an order of two lines with a twenty-one per cent tax under per-line rounding
worked_examples.narrative: The untaxed total is 93.31 plus 134.97, that is 228.28; the tax total is 19.60 plus 28.34, that is 47.94; and the total is 276.22.

records.name: Document amounts under per-line tax rounding
records.purpose: Gives the variant in which the tax engine rounds each line's tax before adding them up, which is what a company that has chosen per-line tax rounding produces.

operands.name: ordered quantity of each line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the order lines
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: unit price of each line
operands.unit_or_currency: the order currency per line unit
operands.source: the order lines
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: discount percentage of each line
operands.source: the order lines
operands.constraints: from 0 to 100 in ordinary use

operands.name: tax rate of each line
operands.source: the tax set of the order line
operands.constraints: the worked example uses a rate of 21 that is not included in the price

operands.name: rounding step of the order currency
operands.source: the currency record
operands.constraints: 0.01 in the worked example

preconditions.condition: The company's tax rounding method is per line.
preconditions.otherwise: The global variant applies instead, and the document tax is rounded once over the summed bases.

preconditions.condition: The taxes are not included in the price.
preconditions.otherwise: An included tax is extracted from the price first, which changes the base but not the ordering of the roundings.

procedure: For each line, compute the untaxed base as the quantity multiplied by the unit price multiplied by one minus the discount fraction.
Round that base to the order currency, giving the line subtotal.
Multiply the rounded line subtotal by the tax rate and round the product to the order currency, giving the line tax.
Add the line subtotal and the line tax, giving the line total.
Sum the line subtotals into the untaxed total, the line taxes into the tax total, and the line totals into the document total.
records.formula: per line : line_subtotal = round_to_currency( quantity × unit_price × ( 1 − discount ÷ 100 ) ) ; line_tax = round_to_currency( line_subtotal × tax_rate ) ; line_total = line_subtotal + line_tax ; document : amount_untaxed = Σ line_subtotal ; amount_tax = Σ line_tax ; amount_total = Σ line_total

rounding.what: Each line's base and each line's tax, separately, before they are summed.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the order currency, 0.01 in the worked example.
rounding.step: Twice per line: once on the base to obtain the subtotal, and once on the tax; the sums are not rounded again.

result.name: untaxed total, tax total and document total
result.unit_or_currency: the order currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the header amount fields of the purchase order.

edge_cases.case: Two lines whose unrounded bases each end in a half step.
edge_cases.outcome: Each is rounded before the addition, so the untaxed total can differ by one step from rounding the summed bases; this is exactly the divergence the company setting selects between.

edge_cases.case: A line with a zero base.
edge_cases.outcome: Its subtotal, tax and total are all zero and it contributes nothing to the sums.

edge_cases.case: A tax that is included in the price.
edge_cases.outcome: The engine extracts it from the price before the base is formed; the two roundings still happen per line.

worked_examples.description: Two lines, per-line rounding, a tax rate of twenty-one per cent
worked_examples.narrative: Line one has a base of seven multiplied by 13.33, that is 93.31, whose tax is 93.31 multiplied by 0.21, that is 19.5951, rounded to 19.60, giving a total of 112.91. Line two has a discounted unit price of 44.991 and a base of 134.973, rounded to a subtotal of 134.97, whose tax is 28.3437 rounded to 28.34, giving a total of 163.31. The header sums to 228.28 untaxed, 47.94 of tax and 276.22 in all.

records.name: Document amounts under global tax rounding
records.purpose: Gives the variant in which the tax engine adds the unrounded bases of every line and rounds the document's tax once, which is what a company that has chosen global tax rounding produces.

operands.name: ordered quantity of each line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the order lines
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: unit price of each line
operands.unit_or_currency: the order currency per line unit
operands.source: the order lines
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: discount percentage of each line
operands.source: the order lines
operands.constraints: from 0 to 100 in ordinary use

operands.name: tax rate of each line
operands.source: the tax set of the order line
operands.constraints: the worked example uses a rate of 21 that is not included in the price

operands.name: rounding step of the order currency
operands.source: the currency record
operands.constraints: 0.01 in the worked example

preconditions.condition: The company's tax rounding method is global.
preconditions.otherwise: The per-line variant applies instead, and each line's tax is rounded before the addition.

preconditions.condition: The whole set of base lines was handed to the engine in one call.
preconditions.otherwise: The engine cannot round globally, because it would see one line at a time; this is why purchasing hands over the whole set at once.

procedure: For each line, compute the untaxed base as the quantity multiplied by the unit price multiplied by one minus the discount fraction, and keep it unrounded.
Add the unrounded bases of every non-display line into the document base.
Multiply the document base by the tax rate and round that single product to the order currency, giving the document tax.
Round the document base to the order currency, giving the untaxed total.
Add the untaxed total and the document tax, giving the document total.
records.formula: amount_untaxed = round_to_currency( Σ over lines of quantity × unit_price × ( 1 − discount ÷ 100 ) ) ; amount_tax = round_to_currency( ( Σ over lines of quantity × unit_price × ( 1 − discount ÷ 100 ) ) × tax_rate ) ; amount_total = amount_untaxed + amount_tax

rounding.what: The summed base and the summed tax of the whole document, each once.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the order currency, 0.01 in the worked example.
rounding.step: Once for the document base and once for the document tax, after every line's base has been added at full precision.

result.name: untaxed total, tax total and document total
result.unit_or_currency: the order currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the header amount fields of the purchase order.

edge_cases.case: Every line's base is already a whole number of currency steps.
edge_cases.outcome: The two variants agree exactly, and the choice of method makes no observable difference for that document.

edge_cases.case: Many small lines whose bases each carry a fraction of a step.
edge_cases.outcome: The fractions accumulate before the single rounding, so the document tax can differ from the per-line sum by one or more steps.

edge_cases.case: A document with one line only.
edge_cases.outcome: The two variants agree, because there is nothing to accumulate.

worked_examples.description: The same two lines under global rounding
worked_examples.narrative: The unrounded bases add to 228.283; the tax is 228.283 multiplied by 0.21, that is 47.93943, rounded once to 47.94. The untaxed total is 228.28 and the document total is 276.22 — the same figures as the per-line variant produces for this document, which is why the two methods must be compared on documents where they diverge rather than on this one.

records.name: The discounted unit price of a line
records.purpose: Gives the unit price after the line's discount, which is the starting figure of the value handed to a goods movement, of the gross unit price and of the accrued-expense amount.

operands.name: unit price of the line
operands.unit_or_currency: the order currency per line unit
operands.source: the unit price field of the order line
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: discount percentage of the line
operands.source: the discount field of the order line
operands.constraints: from 0 to 100 in ordinary use

preconditions.condition: The line carries a unit price.
preconditions.otherwise: The price is treated as zero and the discounted price is zero as well.

procedure: Divide the discount percentage by one hundred.
Subtract that fraction from one.
Multiply the unit price by the result, leaving the product unrounded.
records.formula: price_unit_discounted = price_unit × ( 1 − discount ÷ 100 )

rounding.what: Nothing at this step.
rounding.precision: Not applicable at this step; the figure is carried forward at full precision.
rounding.step: The rounding belongs to whichever computation consumes the discounted price: the goods movement value rounds to the Product Price precision, the line subtotal rounds to the order currency.

result.name: discounted unit price
result.unit_or_currency: the order currency per line unit
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the order line and carried into the value handed to a goods movement, the gross unit price and the accrued-expense amount.

edge_cases.case: The discount is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The discounted price equals the unit price.

edge_cases.case: The discount is 100.
edge_cases.outcome: The discounted price is zero, which is legal and gives a subtotal of zero.

edge_cases.case: The discount is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The retained fraction exceeds one and the discounted price is above the unit price; the arithmetic is applied unchanged.

edge_cases.case: A discount exists at billing time.
edge_cases.outcome: The stored and computed unit prices of the bill line then differ at the Product Price precision, and that difference suppresses the price-difference adjustment.

worked_examples.description: A price of 120.00 per box with a five per cent discount
worked_examples.narrative: One minus five divided by one hundred is 0.95, and 120.00 multiplied by 0.95 is 114.00 per box.

records.name: The unit price restated into the product reference unit
records.purpose: Gives the line's unit price expressed per reference unit of the product, so that lines bought in different units can be compared and reported on one scale.

operands.name: unit price of the line
operands.unit_or_currency: the order currency per line unit
operands.source: the unit price field of the order line
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the unit field of the order line
operands.constraints: must belong to the category of the product reference unit

operands.name: reference unit of measure of the product
operands.source: the product record
operands.constraints: must exist

preconditions.condition: The line is not a display line.
preconditions.otherwise: The restated price is zero.

preconditions.condition: The line is not a down-payment line.
preconditions.otherwise: The restated price is zero, because a down payment carries an amount rather than a price per unit.

procedure: Take the line's unit price.
Convert it from the line unit into the reference unit of the product, using the price conversion, which multiplies by the factor of the target unit and divides by the factor of the source unit.
Leave the result unrounded; it is a displayed and reported figure, not a stored monetary amount.
Return zero instead for a display line and for a down-payment line.
records.formula: price_unit_in_product_unit = convert_price( price_unit , line_unit , product_reference_unit ) , and 0 for a display line or a down-payment line

rounding.what: Nothing at this step.
rounding.precision: Not applicable; the restated price keeps full precision.
rounding.step: Any rounding is applied by the report or the field that displays the figure.

result.name: unit price per reference unit of the product
result.unit_or_currency: the order currency per reference unit of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the order line and used by reporting to compare lines bought in different units.

edge_cases.case: The line unit is the product reference unit.
edge_cases.outcome: The conversion factor is one and the restated price equals the unit price.

edge_cases.case: The line is a display line.
edge_cases.outcome: The restated price is zero, in keeping with the invariant that a display line carries no price.

edge_cases.case: The line is a down-payment line.
edge_cases.outcome: The restated price is zero.

edge_cases.case: The line unit and the product reference unit belong to different categories.
edge_cases.outcome: The conversion is refused; the line could not have been saved with such a unit, because the unit must belong to the product's category.

worked_examples.description: A price per box restated per unit
worked_examples.narrative: A box holds twelve units, so a price of 120.00 per box is 10.00 per unit.

records.name: The company-currency subtotal of a line
records.purpose: Restates a line's subtotal in the company currency so that competing offers priced in different currencies can be compared on one scale.

operands.name: subtotal of the line
operands.source: the computed subtotal of the order line
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: currency rate of the order
operands.source: the stored rate of the order, from the company currency to the order currency
operands.constraints: strictly positive; one when the two currencies coincide

preconditions.condition: The order carries a currency rate.
preconditions.otherwise: The rate is one and the company subtotal equals the line subtotal.

preconditions.condition: The rate is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The division is undefined; a rate is always strictly positive, and a rebuild must treat a zero rate as a configuration error rather than dividing by it.

procedure: Take the line subtotal, which is expressed in the order currency.
Divide it by the order's currency rate, which is the rate from the company currency to the order currency; dividing therefore brings the amount back into the company currency.
Store the quotient as the line's company subtotal, in the company currency.
records.formula: price_total_in_company_currency = price_subtotal ÷ currency_rate

rounding.what: The company subtotal when it is written.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: Once, when the field is written; the division itself is carried at full precision.

result.name: company-currency subtotal of the line
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the line and used by the alternative-order comparison to rank competing offers.

edge_cases.case: The order currency equals the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate is one and the company subtotal equals the subtotal.

edge_cases.case: The subtotal is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The company subtotal is negative by the same ratio.

edge_cases.case: Two offers in two different currencies.
edge_cases.outcome: Each is divided by its own order's rate, so the comparison is made on company-currency figures and not on the raw order-currency amounts.

worked_examples.description: An offer of five hundred units at eleven in a foreign currency
worked_examples.narrative: The subtotal in the order currency is 5 500.00, and dividing by the order rate of 1.1458333… gives 4 800.00 in the company currency.

records.name: The order currency rate
records.purpose: Fixes the single rate an order stores, from the company currency to the order currency at the order deadline, which every company-currency restatement of the order divides by.

operands.name: company currency
operands.source: the company of the order
operands.constraints: must exist

operands.name: order currency
operands.source: the currency field of the order
operands.constraints: must exist

operands.name: company of the order
operands.source: the company field of the order
operands.constraints: must exist

operands.name: order deadline
operands.source: the order deadline field, failing that the current moment
operands.constraints: reduced to its date part for the rate lookup

preconditions.condition: The order has a currency, a company and a deadline.
preconditions.otherwise: The current moment is used in place of a missing deadline, and the rate cannot be computed at all without a currency and a company.

procedure: Take the date part of the order deadline, or of the current moment when the order has no deadline.
Look up the conversion rate from the company currency to the order currency for the order's company on that date.
Store the rate with full precision and no rounding at all.
Recompute it whenever the currency, the order deadline or the company of the order changes.
records.formula: currency_rate = conversion_rate( from = company_currency , to = order_currency , company = order_company , date = date_part( date_order or now ) )

rounding.what: Nothing: the rate is stored at full precision.
rounding.precision: Not applicable; no rounding is applied to the rate itself.
rounding.step: Never; rounding happens only when an amount converted with this rate is written.

result.name: currency rate of the order
result.unit_or_currency: a ratio of the order currency to the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the order and used to restate line subtotals into the company currency and to convert the approval threshold.

edge_cases.case: The order currency equals the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate is one.

edge_cases.case: The order deadline is changed after confirmation.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate is recomputed at the new date, and every company-currency restatement that divides by it changes accordingly.

edge_cases.case: No rate is on file for that date.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate lookup falls back to the nearest earlier rate, and to one when none exists.

edge_cases.case: The order deadline carries a time of day.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the date part is used, so two orders deadlined on the same day share a rate whatever the time.

worked_examples.description: An order deadlined on a day whose rate is one and a quarter
worked_examples.narrative: The rate of the order currency divided by the rate of the company currency is 1.25, so one company-currency unit buys 1.25 order-currency units and the stored rate is 1.25.

records.name: The double-validation threshold restated in the order currency
records.purpose: Converts the company's double-validation amount into the order's currency so that the approval test compares two figures in one currency.

operands.name: double-validation amount of the company
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the active company
operands.source: the company setting for the second approval
operands.constraints: may be zero, which makes every order require the second approval

operands.name: currency of the active company
operands.source: the company the acting user is working in
operands.constraints: must exist; note that it is the active company's currency, not the order company's

operands.name: currency of the order
operands.source: the currency field of the order
operands.constraints: must exist

operands.name: company of the order
operands.source: the company field of the order
operands.constraints: must exist; its rate table is the one consulted

operands.name: order deadline
operands.source: the order deadline field, failing that today
operands.constraints: reduced to its date part

preconditions.condition: The company's approval policy is the two-step policy.
preconditions.otherwise: No threshold is needed, because every order may be approved in one step.

preconditions.condition: A rate exists between the two currencies for the order's company on that date.
preconditions.otherwise: The rate falls back to the nearest earlier rate, and to one when none exists, so the threshold passes through unchanged.

procedure: Take the double-validation amount configured on the company.
Convert it from the active company's currency into the order's currency, for the order's company, at the date part of the order deadline, or today when the order has no deadline.
Compare the order's total with the converted threshold using a strict less-than test.
records.formula: threshold_in_order_currency = convert( company.double_validation_amount , from = active_company_currency , to = order_currency , company = order_company , date = date_part( date_order ) or today )

rounding.what: The converted threshold.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the order currency.
rounding.step: Once, when the threshold is converted, before the comparison.

result.name: approval threshold expressed in the order currency
result.unit_or_currency: the order currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; computed at the moment the approval test runs.

edge_cases.case: The order currency equals the active company's currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The threshold passes through unchanged.

edge_cases.case: The double-validation amount is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: No order total is strictly below zero except a negative one, so every ordinary order requires the second approval.

edge_cases.case: The rate changes after the order was confirmed.
edge_cases.outcome: The threshold is recomputed at the order deadline's date, which is fixed, so a later rate change does not alter the verdict for an order whose deadline has not moved.

worked_examples.description: A threshold of five thousand in the company currency at a rate of 1.0800
worked_examples.narrative: Five thousand multiplied by 1.0800 is 5 400.00 in the order currency, and that is the figure the order total is compared with.

records.name: Whether the acting user may approve the order
records.purpose: Decides, for one acting user and one order, whether confirmation goes straight through or stops for a second approval.

operands.name: approval policy of the company
operands.source: the company setting, whose stored values are `one_step` (the single-approval policy) and `two_step` (the double-approval policy)
operands.constraints: one of the two stored values

operands.name: total of the order
operands.source: the computed total of the order
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: approval threshold expressed in the order currency
operands.source: the converted double-validation amount
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: privileges of the acting user
operands.source: the access groups of the user attempting the approval
operands.constraints: the purchase administrator privilege overrides both other branches

preconditions.condition: The order is being confirmed or approved by a user.
preconditions.otherwise: The test is not run at all; nothing changes state.

preconditions.condition: The company's approval policy is set.
preconditions.otherwise: The single-approval policy is assumed, and confirmation goes straight through.

procedure: Return that approval is allowed when the company's approval policy is the single-approval policy.

Otherwise, when the policy is the double-approval policy, compare the order total with the threshold converted into the order currency and return that approval is allowed only when the total is strictly below the threshold.
Otherwise, return that approval is allowed when the acting user holds the purchase administrator privilege, which overrides the threshold entirely.
Return that approval is not allowed in every other case, which leaves the order waiting for a second approval.
records.formula: approval_allowed = ( approval_policy = `one_step` ) or ( approval_policy = `two_step` and amount_total < threshold_in_order_currency ) or user_has_privilege( purchase administrator )

rounding.what: Nothing at this step; the threshold was rounded when it was converted.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the order currency, applied to the threshold only.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied to the threshold only.
rounding.step: Before the comparison; the order total is already a stored rounded amount.

result.name: verdict that the acting user may approve
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, the result is a yes or no answer
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it decides whether confirmation lands in the purchase status or in the awaiting-approval status.

edge_cases.case: The order total is exactly the threshold.
edge_cases.outcome: The comparison is a strict less-than, so approval is not allowed and the order stops for a second approval.

edge_cases.case: The order total is one currency step below the threshold.
edge_cases.outcome: Approval is allowed and confirmation goes straight through.

edge_cases.case: The acting user holds the purchase administrator privilege.
edge_cases.outcome: Approval is allowed whatever the total.

edge_cases.case: An approval is attempted by a user for whom the test fails.
edge_cases.outcome: The order is filtered out silently: nothing happens and no message is shown.

worked_examples.description: Three totals against a threshold of five thousand four hundred
worked_examples.narrative: A total of 5 399.99 is strictly below 5 400.00 and goes straight to the purchase status. A total of exactly 5 400.00 is not strictly below the threshold and stops for a second approval, as does 5 400.01. A purchase administrator would be allowed to approve all three.

records.name: The expected arrival of an order line
records.purpose: Computes the date on which a line's goods are expected, from the order deadline and the vendor's lead time, which drives the receipt schedule and the punctuality figures.

operands.name: order deadline
operands.source: the order deadline field, failing that the current moment
operands.constraints: a timestamp carrying a time of day

operands.name: lead time of the selected vendor price
operands.source: the vendor pricelist entry selected for the line, failing that zero
operands.constraints: a whole or fractional number of days, never negative in ordinary configuration

preconditions.condition: The line is not a display line.
preconditions.otherwise: No expected arrival is computed and the line stores none, in keeping with the invariant that a display line carries no arrival date.

preconditions.condition: The line has no bill line yet.
preconditions.otherwise: Every automatic date computation is suppressed for that line for good, and the stored arrival is left as it is.

procedure: Take the order deadline, or the current moment when the order has none.
Take the lead time in days of the vendor price selected for the line, or zero when no vendor price was selected.
Add that number of calendar days to the timestamp, preserving the time of day and consulting no working calendar at all.
Store the result as the line's expected arrival.
records.formula: line.date_planned = ( date_order or now ) + ( lead time of the selected vendor price or 0 ) days

rounding.what: Nothing: the result is a timestamp, not a decimal figure.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.method: Not applicable; the addition is a plain calendar-day addition.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: expected arrival of the line
result.unit_or_currency: a timestamp
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the order line, shown on the order form, and used by the header arrival, by the punctuality figures and by the grouping windows.

edge_cases.case: The line has no selected vendor price.
edge_cases.outcome: The lead time is zero and the expected arrival equals the order deadline.

edge_cases.case: The addition crosses a weekend or a public holiday.
edge_cases.outcome: It still lands on that day: no working calendar is consulted and no day is skipped.

edge_cases.case: The order deadline carries a time of day.
edge_cases.outcome: The time of day is preserved exactly, so an order deadlined at 09:15 gives arrivals at 09:15.

edge_cases.case: The order's expected arrival is written from the form.
edge_cases.outcome: Every non-display line receives the same value, and the recomputation of the header value from the lines is prevented from flowing back down.

edge_cases.case: A vendor updates the dates through the portal for a line whose movements are all done.
edge_cases.outcome: The line's own expected arrival is not changed, and the activity note says the dates could not be modified on the already validated receipt.

worked_examples.description: Two lines whose vendor lead times are four and ten days
worked_examples.narrative: Four calendar days after the 3rd at 09:15 is the 7th at 09:15, and ten calendar days after it is the 13th at 09:15; both keep the time of day of the order deadline.

records.name: The expected arrival of the order header
records.purpose: Gives the order's single expected arrival, which is the earliest of its lines', and which the reminder job, the late search and the grouping windows all read.

operands.name: expected arrival of each non-display line that has one
operands.source: the expected arrival field of the order lines
operands.constraints: a line without an arrival is skipped; a display line never has one

preconditions.condition: At least one non-display line carries an expected arrival.
preconditions.otherwise: The header arrival is empty, and an order with no expected arrival is never sent a reminder.

procedure: Collect the expected arrivals of the non-display lines that have one.
Take the earliest of them.
Store it as the order's expected arrival, or leave the field empty when no line qualifies.
records.formula: order.date_planned = min over non-display lines that have one ( line.date_planned ) , and empty when no line qualifies

rounding.what: Nothing: the result is a timestamp.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: expected arrival of the order
result.unit_or_currency: a timestamp
