operands.constraints: converted into the product reference unit before it is summed

operands.name: factor of the movement detail's unit and factor of the product reference unit
operands.source: the unit of measure records
operands.constraints: both strictly positive

operands.name: expected arrival of the line
operands.source: the order line
operands.constraints: compared by date part only

operands.name: date of the movement
operands.source: the goods movement holding the detail
operands.constraints: compared by date part only

preconditions.condition: The movement holding the detail is completed.
preconditions.otherwise: The detail contributes zero to the on-time quantity.

preconditions.condition: The line has an expected arrival.
preconditions.otherwise: No comparison can be made and the detail contributes zero.

procedure: Take the line's total quantity as the ordered column of the row.
For each detail of the line's goods movements, check that the movement is completed and that the date part of the line's expected arrival is on or after the date part of the movement's date.

For a detail that passes both checks, restate its quantity into the product reference unit by multiplying by the factor of its own unit and dividing by the factor of the product reference unit, and add the result to the on-time quantity.
For a detail that fails either check, add zero.
records.formula: qty_total = line.total_quantity ; qty_on_time = Σ over the movement details d of ( d.quantity × d.unit_factor ÷ product_unit_factor ) when d's movement is completed and date_part( line.date_planned ) ≥ date_part( movement.date ) , and 0 otherwise

rounding.what: The restated detail quantities.
rounding.precision: The rounding of the product reference unit.
rounding.step: At the restatement of each detail quantity, before it is added.

result.name: ordered quantity and on-time quantity of the row
result.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line for the ordered quantity, the product reference unit for the on-time quantity
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the vendor delay report row and aggregated by the report.

edge_cases.case: A movement dated on the same calendar day as the expected arrival.
edge_cases.outcome: It counts as on time, because the comparison is on date parts and uses an on-or-after test.

edge_cases.case: A movement that is not completed.
edge_cases.outcome: It contributes zero to the on-time quantity but the line's total quantity is unchanged.

edge_cases.case: A line with no completed movement at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The on-time quantity is zero and the row's rate is zero.

edge_cases.case: A detail expressed in a unit other than the product reference unit.
edge_cases.outcome: It is restated before it is added, so the two columns are comparable.

worked_examples.description: A line of one hundred units, half of which arrived on time
worked_examples.narrative: The ordered column is one hundred; only the first detail arrived by the expected arrival, so the on-time column is fifty.

records.name: The aggregated on-time rate of the vendor delay report
records.purpose: Gives the rate a group of vendor delay rows reports, which is a weighted rate rather than an average of the row rates.

operands.name: on-time quantity of each row in the group
operands.source: the rows being aggregated
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: total quantity of each row in the group
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the rows being aggregated
operands.constraints: a row whose summed total quantity is zero is excluded from the grouping

preconditions.condition: The summed total quantity of the group is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The rate is one hundred, which is the value the report shows when there is nothing to be late about.

preconditions.condition: The rows whose summed total quantity is zero have been excluded.
preconditions.otherwise: They would contribute a denominator of zero to the group and distort the rate.

procedure: Exclude from the grouping every row whose summed total quantity is zero.
Sum the on-time quantities of the remaining rows.
Sum the total quantities of the remaining rows.
Divide the first sum by the second and multiply by one hundred; return one hundred instead when the second sum is zero.
records.formula: on_time_rate = Σ qty_on_time ÷ Σ qty_total × 100 when Σ qty_total ≠ 0 , and = 100 otherwise

rounding.what: The rate as it is displayed.
rounding.precision: Two decimal digits as displayed by the report.
rounding.step: At display; the ratio is kept at full precision while it is computed.

result.name: aggregated on-time rate of the group
result.unit_or_currency: a percentage
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed by the vendor delay report for the group; not stored.

edge_cases.case: Every row in the group has a zero total quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The group's summed total quantity is zero and the rate is one hundred.

edge_cases.case: One row is heavily over-delivered.
edge_cases.outcome: The weighted rate can exceed one hundred, because the numerator sums movement quantities and the denominator sums line quantities.

edge_cases.case: A single-row group.
edge_cases.outcome: The aggregated rate equals that row's own rate.

edge_cases.case: Rows with very different sizes.
edge_cases.outcome: The weighting by quantity means a large line dominates the group rate, which is the intended behaviour and differs from averaging the row rates.

worked_examples.description: A group of two rows of very different sizes
worked_examples.narrative: One hundred on time out of four hundred ordered gives twenty-five per cent; averaging the two row rates of one hundred and zero would have given fifty and would have been wrong.

records.name: The dashboard on-time figure
records.purpose: Gives the whole-number percentage of recent orders that arrived by their expected arrival, which the purchasing dashboard shows both for everyone and for the current user.

operands.name: orders whose status is the confirmed status and whose expected arrival falls within the last three months
operands.source: the purchase orders selected for the dashboard
operands.constraints: the denominator of the figure

operands.name: arrival date of each such order
operands.source: the date the goods actually arrived
operands.constraints: compared by date part only

operands.name: expected arrival of each such order
operands.source: the expected arrival of the order
operands.constraints: compared by date part only

preconditions.condition: At least one order matches the selection.
preconditions.otherwise: The figure is one hundred, which is what the dashboard shows when there is nothing to be late about.

preconditions.condition: The selected orders carry an arrival date.
preconditions.otherwise: An order without one does not satisfy the on-time test and counts only in the denominator.

procedure: Select the purchase orders whose status is the confirmed status and whose expected arrival falls within the last three months.
Count them; this is the denominator.
Count those whose arrival date has a date part on or before the date part of their expected arrival; this is the numerator.
Divide the numerator by the denominator, multiply by one hundred and round to a whole number; return one hundred instead when the denominator is zero.
Compute the same figure a second time over the current user's own orders only.
records.formula: on_time_count = count of the selected orders whose arrival date has a date part ≤ the date part of the expected arrival ; on_time_figure = round_to_precision( on_time_count ÷ total_count × 100 , 0 ) , and = 100 when total_count = 0

rounding.what: The percentage.
rounding.precision: Zero decimal digits, that is a whole number.
rounding.step: Once, after the division and the multiplication by one hundred.

result.name: dashboard on-time percentage
result.unit_or_currency: a percentage as a whole number
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the purchasing dashboard, once for every order and once restricted to the current user's own orders.

edge_cases.case: No order matches the selection.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure is one hundred rather than undefined.

edge_cases.case: An order arrived later in the day than its expected arrival but on the same calendar day.
edge_cases.outcome: It counts as on time, because only the date parts are compared.

edge_cases.case: An order has no arrival date at all.
edge_cases.outcome: It counts in the denominator but not in the numerator, so it lowers the figure.

edge_cases.case: The percentage falls exactly on a half.
edge_cases.outcome: It is rounded away from zero, so 85.5 becomes 86.

worked_examples.description: Seven of nine recent orders arrived by their expected arrival
worked_examples.narrative: Seven divided by nine is 0.7777…, multiplied by one hundred is 77.77…, rounded to a whole number is seventy-eight.

records.name: The dashboard days-to-order figure
records.purpose: Gives the average number of days between the creation of an order and its confirmation, which the purchasing dashboard shows both for everyone and for the current user.

operands.name: confirmation date of each selected order
operands.source: the confirmation date field of the order
operands.constraints: an order without one is not selected

operands.name: creation date of each selected order
operands.source: the creation date of the order
operands.constraints: always present

operands.name: count of selected orders
operands.source: the purchase orders whose status is the confirmed status, created within the last three months and carrying a confirmation date
operands.constraints: the divisor of the average

preconditions.condition: At least one order matches the selection.
preconditions.otherwise: The figure is zero.

preconditions.condition: Each selected order carries a confirmation date.
preconditions.otherwise: It is not selected at all.

procedure: Select the purchase orders whose status is the confirmed status, that were created within the last three months and that carry a confirmation date.
For each, subtract the creation date from the confirmation date and express the difference in seconds.
Add the differences and divide by the count of selected orders, giving the average in seconds.
Divide the average by sixty, then by sixty again, then by twenty-four, giving days, and round to two decimal digits.
Return zero when there are no such orders, and compute the same figure again over the current user's own orders, using that user's own count as the divisor.
records.formula: average_seconds = Σ ( date_approve − create_date , in seconds ) ÷ count ; days_to_order = round_to_precision( average_seconds ÷ 60 ÷ 60 ÷ 24 , 2 ) , and 0 when there are no such orders

rounding.what: The average in days.
rounding.precision: Two decimal digits.
rounding.step: Once, at the end, after the average in seconds has been divided down to days.

result.name: average days to order
result.unit_or_currency: days
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the purchasing dashboard, once for every order and once restricted to the current user's own orders.

edge_cases.case: No order matches the selection.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure is zero rather than undefined.

edge_cases.case: An order confirmed within the same hour it was created.
edge_cases.outcome: It contributes a small fraction of a day and pulls the average down.

edge_cases.case: The user-restricted figure.
edge_cases.outcome: It uses that user's own count as the divisor, not the overall count, so the two figures are independent averages.

edge_cases.case: An order that was reset to draft and confirmed again.
edge_cases.outcome: Its confirmation date is not cleared by the reset, so the figure uses the confirmation date it carries.

worked_examples.description: Three orders confirmed two days, five days and half a day after creation
worked_examples.narrative: The three intervals are 172 800, 432 000 and 43 200 seconds; their sum is 648 000 and the average is 216 000 seconds, which divided by sixty, sixty and twenty-four gives 2.50 days.

records.name: The monthly demand of a product
records.purpose: Restates the demand observed over a chosen window as a demand per month, which the replenishment suggestion multiplies by the horizon.

operands.name: demanded quantities of the selected goods movements
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
operands.source: the movements of the product whose status is waiting, ready, confirmed, partially available or completed, whose date falls in the window implied by the basis, and whose direction counts as demand
operands.constraints: summed into one figure

operands.name: basis chosen on the panel
operands.source: the replenishment panel
operands.constraints: one of: one year, three months, the same quarter last year, one week, thirty days, or actual demand

operands.name: factor implied by the basis
operands.source: the basis: 12 for one year, 3 for three months and for the same quarter last year, 7 divided by 365.25 divided by 12 for one week, and 1 for thirty days
operands.constraints: strictly positive

preconditions.condition: The basis is one of the demand bases rather than actual demand.
preconditions.otherwise: The actual-demand branch of the suggested quantity applies instead and no monthly demand is computed.

preconditions.condition: At least one movement falls in the window.
preconditions.otherwise: The demand is zero and the suggested quantity is zero, because the suggestion is zero whenever the monthly demand is not strictly positive.

procedure: Select the goods movements of the product whose status is waiting, ready, confirmed, partially available or completed.
Keep those whose date falls in the window implied by the basis.
Keep those whose direction counts as demand: leaving the selected warehouse, or reaching a customer location, a production location or a transit location.
Sum their demanded quantities.

Divide the sum by the factor implied by the basis: twelve for one year, three for three months and for the same quarter last year, seven divided by 365.25 divided by twelve for one week, and one for thirty days.
records.formula: monthly_demand = Q ÷ factor , where Q is the summed demanded quantity of the selected movements and factor = 12 for one year , 3 for three months or the same quarter last year , 7 ÷ ( 365.25 ÷ 12 ) = 0.2300… for one week , and 1 for thirty days

rounding.what: Nothing at this step; the monthly demand is carried at full precision into the suggested quantity.
rounding.precision: Not applicable at this step.
rounding.step: The rounding happens once, on the suggested quantity, and is a rounding up to whole units.

result.name: monthly demand of the product
result.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product per month
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the suggested quantity.

edge_cases.case: The basis is thirty days, which is the shipped default.
edge_cases.outcome: The factor is one, so the summed demand over the last thirty days is taken as the monthly demand directly.

edge_cases.case: The basis is one week.
edge_cases.outcome: The factor is seven divided by the average month length of 365.25 divided by twelve, that is 0.2300…, so a week's demand is scaled up to a month.

edge_cases.case: The basis is the same quarter last year.
edge_cases.outcome: The window moves back a year but the factor is three, the same as for the last three months.

edge_cases.case: The monthly demand is zero or negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The suggested quantity is zero, whatever the horizon and the percentage.

edge_cases.case: A movement is cancelled or a draft.
edge_cases.outcome: Its status is not among the five selected statuses and it is excluded.

worked_examples.description: Two hundred and sixty units of demand over the last thirty days
worked_examples.narrative: With a factor of one the monthly demand is 260 divided by one, that is two hundred and sixty units a month.

worked_examples.description: A year of demand restated per month
worked_examples.narrative: Three thousand one hundred and twenty units over a year divided by the factor of twelve is two hundred and sixty units a month.

records.name: The suggested quantity under the actual-demand basis
records.purpose: Gives the quantity the replenishment panel suggests when the basis is actual demand, which reads the forecast at the end of the horizon rather than a historical window.

operands.name: forecast quantity at the end of the horizon
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
operands.source: the forecast of the product evaluated at the current moment plus the horizon in days
operands.constraints: may be positive, negative or zero; only a negative forecast produces a suggestion

operands.name: percentage chosen on the panel
operands.source: the replenishment panel
operands.constraints: one hundred means cover the whole shortfall

operands.name: horizon in days
operands.source: the replenishment panel
operands.constraints: the forecast is evaluated at the current moment plus this many days

preconditions.condition: The basis is actual demand.
preconditions.otherwise: The historical-demand variant applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The forecast quantity is strictly negative.
preconditions.otherwise: The suggested quantity is zero, because a forecast that is not negative means nothing is short.

procedure: Evaluate the product's forecast at the current moment plus the horizon in days.
When the forecast is not strictly negative, return a suggestion of zero.
Otherwise negate the forecast, giving the shortfall as a positive quantity.
Multiply the shortfall by the percentage divided by one hundred.
Round the product up to whole units, away from zero, and take the greater of that figure and zero.
records.formula: suggested_qty = max( round_up( − forecast_quantity × p ÷ 100 , 0 ) , 0 ) when forecast_quantity < 0 , and = 0 otherwise

rounding.what: The scaled shortfall.
rounding.precision: Zero decimal digits, that is whole units.
rounding.method: Away from zero, never downwards, so a fractional need always becomes a whole extra unit.
rounding.step: Once, on the scaled shortfall, before the maximum against zero is taken.

result.name: suggested quantity
result.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: Shown on the replenishment panel and carried onto the request for quotation the panel creates.

edge_cases.case: The forecast is exactly zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The suggestion is zero, because the branch requires a strictly negative forecast.

edge_cases.case: The forecast is positive.
edge_cases.outcome: The suggestion is zero.

edge_cases.case: The percentage is below one hundred.
edge_cases.outcome: Only that fraction of the shortfall is suggested, and the rounding up still applies, so a small fraction of a unit still becomes one whole unit.

edge_cases.case: The percentage is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The scaled shortfall is zero, the rounding up leaves it at zero, and the suggestion is zero.

worked_examples.description: A forecast short by twenty-four and three-quarters units, covered in full
worked_examples.narrative: The forecast is minus 24.75, so the shortfall is 24.75; at one hundred per cent the scaled shortfall is 24.75, which rounds up to twenty-five whole units.

worked_examples.description: The same forecast covered at half
worked_examples.narrative: Half of 24.75 is 12.375, which rounds up to thirteen whole units.

records.name: The suggested quantity under every basis other than actual demand
records.purpose: Gives the quantity the replenishment panel suggests from a historical demand, after covering the horizon and deducting what is already on hand and already incoming.

operands.name: monthly demand of the product
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product per month
operands.source: the demand summed over the window implied by the basis, divided by the basis factor
operands.constraints: the suggestion is zero when it is not strictly positive

operands.name: horizon in days
operands.source: the replenishment panel
operands.constraints: strictly positive in ordinary use

operands.name: percentage chosen on the panel
operands.source: the replenishment panel
operands.constraints: one hundred means cover the whole computed need

operands.name: on-hand quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
operands.source: the current stock of the product in the selected warehouse
operands.constraints: only a positive on-hand quantity is deducted

operands.name: incoming quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
operands.source: the quantity already expected to arrive
operands.constraints: only a positive incoming quantity is deducted

preconditions.condition: The basis is one of the historical-demand bases.
preconditions.otherwise: The actual-demand variant applies instead.

preconditions.condition: The monthly demand is strictly positive.
preconditions.otherwise: The suggested quantity is zero, whatever the horizon, the percentage, the on-hand quantity and the incoming quantity.

procedure: Divide the horizon in days by the average month length of 365.25 divided by twelve, giving the monthly ratio, that is the fraction of a month the horizon covers.
Multiply the monthly demand by the monthly ratio and by the percentage divided by one hundred, giving the need over the horizon.
Subtract the greater of the on-hand quantity and zero, so that a negative on-hand quantity does not inflate the need.
Subtract the greater of the incoming quantity and zero, on the same principle.
Round the remainder up to whole units, away from zero, and take the greater of that figure and zero.
records.formula: monthly_ratio = h ÷ ( 365.25 ÷ 12 ) ; raw = monthly_demand × monthly_ratio × p ÷ 100 − max( on_hand_quantity , 0 ) − max( incoming_quantity , 0 ) ; suggested_qty = max( round_up( raw , 0 ) , 0 ) , and 0 whenever the monthly demand is not strictly positive

rounding.what: The raw need, after the two deductions.
rounding.precision: Zero decimal digits, that is whole units.
rounding.step: Once, on the raw need, before the maximum against zero is taken.

result.name: suggested quantity
result.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: Shown on the replenishment panel and carried onto the request for quotation the panel creates.

edge_cases.case: The on-hand and incoming quantities already cover the need.
edge_cases.outcome: The raw need is negative, the rounding up moves it further from zero, and the maximum against zero returns a suggestion of zero.

edge_cases.case: The on-hand quantity is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The greater of it and zero is zero, so a negative stock does not inflate the suggestion.

edge_cases.case: The monthly demand is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The suggestion is zero without any further arithmetic.

edge_cases.case: The horizon is longer than a month.
edge_cases.outcome: The monthly ratio exceeds one and the need is more than one month's demand.

edge_cases.case: The percentage is above one hundred.
edge_cases.outcome: The need is inflated in proportion, which is how a safety margin is expressed.

worked_examples.description: A monthly demand of two hundred and sixty over a seven-day horizon at one hundred per cent
worked_examples.narrative: Seven divided by 30.4375 is 0.229938…, and two hundred and sixty multiplied by it at one hundred per cent is 59.784. Deducting twenty on hand and fifteen incoming leaves a raw need of 24.784, which rounds up to twenty-five units.

worked_examples.description: The same figures at fifty per cent
worked_examples.narrative: Half the need is 29.892, and deducting thirty-five leaves minus 5.108, so the maximum against zero gives a suggestion of zero.

records.name: The suggested estimated price of a replenishment suggestion
records.purpose: Values a replenishment suggestion so that the panel can show what the suggested purchase would cost.

operands.name: suggested quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
operands.source: the computed replenishment suggestion
operands.constraints: the value is zero when it is not positive

operands.name: discounted price of the vendor pricelist entry selected for the suggested quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the vendor pricelist entry per reference unit
operands.source: the vendor pricelist of the product
operands.constraints: used first when such an entry exists

operands.name: discounted price of the vendor pricelist entry with the smallest minimum quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the vendor pricelist entry per reference unit
operands.source: the vendor pricelist of the product
operands.constraints: used when no entry qualifies for the suggested quantity

operands.name: cost of the product
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the product record
operands.constraints: used when the vendor pricelist offers nothing at all

preconditions.condition: The suggested quantity is strictly positive.
preconditions.otherwise: The estimated price is zero.

preconditions.condition: A price can be resolved from the vendor pricelist or from the product.
preconditions.otherwise: The product cost is the last resort and always exists, so a price is always resolvable.

procedure: Return zero when the suggested quantity is not positive.

Otherwise resolve the price: take the discounted price of the vendor pricelist entry selected for the suggested quantity; failing that, the discounted price of the entry with the smallest minimum quantity; failing that, the product's cost.
Multiply the suggested quantity by the resolved price.
Show the product as the estimated price of the suggestion.
records.formula: suggest_estimated_price = suggested_qty × price , where price is the discounted price of the vendor pricelist entry selected for the suggested quantity , failing that the discounted price of the entry with the smallest minimum quantity , failing that the product's cost ; and the value is 0 when the suggested quantity is not positive

rounding.what: The estimated price as it is displayed.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the currency it is displayed in.
rounding.step: At display; the multiplication itself is not rounded.

result.name: estimated price of the suggestion
result.unit_or_currency: the currency of the resolved price
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the replenishment panel; not stored on any order until the panel creates one.

edge_cases.case: The suggested quantity is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The estimated price is zero and no price is resolved at all.

edge_cases.case: The vendor has an entry but none qualifies for the suggested quantity or the date.
edge_cases.outcome: The entry with the smallest minimum quantity is used, which is the cheapest available approximation of the vendor's price.

edge_cases.case: The product has no vendor pricelist entry at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The product's cost is used.

edge_cases.case: The vendor pricelist entry carries a discount.
edge_cases.outcome: The discounted price is used, not the list price.

worked_examples.description: Twenty-five units at a discounted vendor price of four

inputs.price_source: the vendor pricelist entry selected for the quantity

worked_examples.narrative: Twenty-five multiplied by 4.00 is 100.00.

records.name: The daily grouping window
records.purpose: Gives the window an existing request for quotation's expected arrival must fall in for a procurement need to join it, under the daily grouping policy.

operands.name: requested arrival timestamp of the procurement need
operands.source: the procurement need being grouped
operands.constraints: the anchor of the window

operands.name: expected arrival of the candidate existing order
operands.source: the request for quotation being considered
operands.constraints: must fall inside the window for the order to accept the need

preconditions.condition: The vendor's grouping policy is the daily policy.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the other four policies applies and the window is different or absent.

preconditions.condition: The procurement need carries a requested arrival.
preconditions.otherwise: No window can be formed and the need starts a new order.

procedure: Take the date part of the requested arrival.
Set the start of the window to that date at 00:00:00.
Set the end of the window to the same date at 23:59:59.999999.
Accept an existing order whose expected arrival falls inside that window, and start a new order otherwise.
records.formula: window = [ date_part( requested_date ) at 00:00:00 , date_part( requested_date ) at 23:59:59.999999 ]

rounding.what: Nothing: the window is a pair of timestamps.
rounding.precision: The window's end is expressed to the microsecond, at 23:59:59.999999.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: accepted window for the candidate order's expected arrival
result.unit_or_currency: a pair of timestamps
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; used to decide whether an existing request for quotation absorbs the procurement need.

edge_cases.case: The candidate's expected arrival is on the same day but at a different time.
edge_cases.outcome: It falls inside the window and the order accepts the need.

edge_cases.case: The candidate's expected arrival is one microsecond after the end of the window.
edge_cases.outcome: It falls outside and a new order is started.

edge_cases.case: Several candidates fall inside the window.
edge_cases.outcome: The grouping picks one of them; the window only decides eligibility.

worked_examples.description: A need requested on the 14th at 08:00
worked_examples.narrative: The window is the whole of the 14th, so a candidate order expecting arrival at any time on the 14th accepts the need.

records.name: The weekly grouping window without a target week day
records.purpose: Gives the seven-day window an existing request for quotation's expected arrival must fall in when the vendor groups weekly and no target week day is configured.

operands.name: requested arrival timestamp of the procurement need
operands.source: the procurement need being grouped
operands.constraints: the anchor of the window

operands.name: day-of-week index of the requested arrival
operands.source: the requested arrival, with Monday counted as 1 and Sunday as 7
operands.constraints: a whole number from 1 to 7

operands.name: expected arrival of the candidate existing order
operands.source: the request for quotation being considered
operands.constraints: must fall inside the window

preconditions.condition: The vendor's grouping policy is the weekly policy and no target week day is configured.
preconditions.otherwise: The variant with a target week day applies instead, and the window is a single day.

preconditions.condition: The procurement need carries a requested arrival.
preconditions.otherwise: No window can be formed and the need starts a new order.

procedure: Compute the day-of-week index of the requested arrival, with Monday counted as one and Sunday as seven.
Subtract that index in days from the requested arrival and take the resulting date at 00:00:00 as the start of the window.
Add six minus that index in days to the requested arrival and take the resulting date at 23:59:59.999999 as the end of the window.
Accept an existing order whose expected arrival falls inside that window, and start a new order otherwise.
records.formula: window = [ ( requested_date − weekday( requested_date ) days ) at 00:00:00 , ( requested_date + ( 6 − weekday( requested_date ) ) days ) at 23:59:59.999999 ] , with Monday = 1 and Sunday = 7

rounding.what: Nothing: the window is a pair of timestamps.
rounding.precision: The window's end is expressed to the microsecond.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: accepted window for the candidate order's expected arrival
result.unit_or_currency: a pair of timestamps
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; used to decide whether an existing request for quotation absorbs the procurement need.

edge_cases.case: The requested arrival falls on a Monday, whose index is one.
edge_cases.outcome: The window starts on the Sunday before and ends on the Saturday, spanning seven days.

edge_cases.case: The requested arrival falls on a Sunday, whose index is seven.
edge_cases.outcome: The window starts seven days earlier, on the previous Sunday, and ends on the Saturday of that same span, so the requested day is the last of the window.

edge_cases.case: The window is described as a week but does not start on a Monday.
edge_cases.outcome: Subtracting the day-of-week index from a Wednesday lands two days before the Monday, so the window starts on the Sunday; this is the behaviour as observed and a rebuild must reproduce it to group the same needs onto the same orders.

edge_cases.case: A candidate's expected arrival falls one day outside the window.
edge_cases.outcome: It is rejected and the need either finds another candidate or starts a new order.

worked_examples.description: A need requested on Wednesday the 14th
worked_examples.narrative: The day-of-week index of a Wednesday is three, so the window starts three days earlier, on Sunday the 11th at midnight, and ends six minus three, that is three days later, on Saturday the 17th at the last microsecond of the day.

records.name: The weekly grouping window with a target week day
records.purpose: Gives the single accepted day when the vendor groups weekly onto a chosen week day, and the forward shift the new line and the order deadline then take.

operands.name: requested arrival timestamp of the procurement need
operands.source: the procurement need being grouped
operands.constraints: the anchor of the offset

operands.name: day-of-week index of the requested arrival
operands.source: the requested arrival, with Monday counted as 1 and Sunday as 7
operands.constraints: a whole number from 1 to 7

operands.name: target week day
operands.source: the vendor's grouping configuration
operands.constraints: a whole number from 1 to 7

operands.name: expected arrival of the candidate existing order
operands.source: the request for quotation being considered
operands.constraints: must fall on the single accepted day

preconditions.condition: The vendor's grouping policy is the weekly policy and a target week day is configured.
preconditions.otherwise: The variant without a target week day applies instead, and the window spans seven days.

preconditions.condition: The procurement need carries a requested arrival.
preconditions.otherwise: No offset can be computed and the need starts a new order.

procedure: Compute the day-of-week index of the requested arrival, with Monday counted as one and Sunday as seven.
Add seven to the target week day, subtract the day-of-week index, and take the remainder on division by seven; this is the offset in days, which is never negative and never reaches seven.
Add the offset in days to the requested arrival; the single accepted day is that date, from 00:00:00 to 23:59:59.999999.
Push the new line's expected arrival forward to that day.
When the order's own expected arrival is not earlier than the new one, push the order deadline forward by the same number of days.
records.formula: δ = ( 7 + target_weekday − weekday( requested_date ) ) mod 7 ; accepted day = requested_date + δ days , from 00:00:00 to 23:59:59.999999

rounding.what: Nothing: the offset is a whole number of days and the window is a pair of timestamps.
rounding.precision: The window's end is expressed to the microsecond.
rounding.method: Not applicable; the remainder on division by seven is exact.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: offset in days and the single accepted day
result.unit_or_currency: days and a pair of timestamps
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored as such; the accepted day becomes the new line's expected arrival, and the offset may move the order deadline.

edge_cases.case: The target week day equals the requested arrival's own week day.
edge_cases.outcome: The offset is zero and the accepted day is the requested day itself.

edge_cases.case: The target week day is earlier in the week than the requested day.
edge_cases.outcome: Adding seven before the remainder is taken makes the offset positive, so the accepted day is the next such week day and never the one already past.

edge_cases.case: The order's own expected arrival is earlier than the new line's.
edge_cases.outcome: The order deadline is left where it is, and only the line's arrival moves.

edge_cases.case: The order's own expected arrival is not earlier than the new line's.
edge_cases.outcome: The order deadline is pushed forward by the same number of days as the line's arrival.

worked_examples.description: A need requested on Wednesday the 14th with a target of Friday
worked_examples.narrative: Seven plus five minus three is nine, whose remainder on division by seven is two, so the accepted day is Friday the 16th; the new line's expected arrival is pushed forward to the 16th and, if the order's own expected arrival is not earlier, the order deadline moves forward by the same two days.

worked_examples.description: The same need with a target of Monday
worked_examples.narrative: Seven plus one minus three is five, whose remainder on division by seven is five, so the accepted day is Monday the 19th, the next Monday and never the one already past.

records.name: Grouping without a date window
records.purpose: Fixes the two grouping policies that apply no date window at all, and states the reference test that replaces the window under the on-order policy.

operands.name: grouping policy of the vendor
operands.source: the vendor's grouping configuration
operands.constraints: one of the on-order policy and the always policy in this variant

operands.name: procurement references of the candidate existing order
operands.source: the request for quotation being considered
operands.constraints: compared with the procurement's own references under the on-order policy

operands.name: procurement references of the need
operands.source: the procurement need being grouped
operands.constraints: may be absent, in which case the candidate must carry none either

preconditions.condition: The vendor's grouping policy is the on-order policy or the always policy.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the three dated policies applies and a date window is formed.

preconditions.condition: Under the on-order policy the candidate carries the same procurement references, or carries none when the procurement has none.
preconditions.otherwise: The candidate is rejected and the need either finds another candidate or starts a new order.

procedure: Under the on-order policy, apply no date window at all; instead require that the candidate order carry the same procurement references as the need, or carry no reference at all when the need has none.
Under the always policy, apply no date window and no reference test, so any existing order of the vendor may absorb the need.
Accept the first candidate that satisfies the test, and start a new order when none does.
records.formula: on-order policy : no date window ; the candidate must carry the same procurement references , or none when the procurement has none ; always policy : no date window and no further test

rounding.what: Nothing: the test is a comparison of references, not of numbers.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: verdict that the candidate order may absorb the need
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, the result is a yes or no answer
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it decides whether a new request for quotation is created.

edge_cases.case: The need has no procurement reference and the candidate carries one.
edge_cases.outcome: The candidate is rejected under the on-order policy, because the need with no reference requires a candidate with none.

edge_cases.case: The always policy with several open orders for the vendor.
edge_cases.outcome: Any of them may absorb the need, so the grouping is the widest of the five.

edge_cases.case: The on-order policy with matching references but very different arrival dates.
edge_cases.outcome: The candidate is still accepted, because no date window applies.

worked_examples.description: A need with no procurement reference under the on-order policy
worked_examples.narrative: The need carries no reference, so only a candidate that carries none may absorb it; the candidate carrying a reference is rejected.

records.name: The order deadline chosen for a new order
records.purpose: Gives the deadline a newly created request for quotation takes when several procurement needs are grouped onto it.

operands.name: explicit order date of each procurement in the group
operands.source: the procurement need, when it names one
operands.constraints: used in preference to the derived date

operands.name: requested arrival of each procurement in the group
operands.source: the procurement need
operands.constraints: used when no explicit order date is named

operands.name: vendor lead time
operands.source: the vendor pricelist entry selected for the product
operands.constraints: subtracted from the requested arrival to derive an order date

preconditions.condition: The group holds at least one procurement.
preconditions.otherwise: No order is created and no deadline is chosen.

preconditions.condition: Each procurement names either an explicit order date or a requested arrival.
preconditions.otherwise: No candidate date can be formed for that procurement and it contributes none to the minimum.

procedure: For each procurement in the group, form a candidate date: its explicit order date when it names one, otherwise its requested arrival minus the vendor lead time in days.
Take the earliest of those candidate dates.
Set the new order's deadline to that earliest date, so that the order is placed early enough for the most urgent need in the group.
records.formula: date_order = min over the group's procurements of ( explicit_order_date , or requested_arrival − vendor_lead_time days )

rounding.what: Nothing: the result is a timestamp.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.method: Not applicable; the subtraction is a plain calendar-day subtraction.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: order deadline of the new request for quotation
result.unit_or_currency: a timestamp
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the new purchase order and used as the base of every line's expected arrival.

edge_cases.case: One procurement names an explicit order date earlier than every derived date.
edge_cases.outcome: That explicit date becomes the deadline.

edge_cases.case: The vendor has no lead time.
edge_cases.outcome: The lead time is zero and the candidate date equals the requested arrival.

edge_cases.case: The group holds one procurement only.
edge_cases.outcome: Its own candidate date is the deadline.

edge_cases.case: A later line is added whose derived deadline is earlier.
edge_cases.outcome: The deadline is pulled back, by the separate rule that pulls it back for a new line.

worked_examples.description: Two procurements with lead times of seven and two days
worked_examples.narrative: The first procurement needs the order placed on the 23rd and the second on the 26th; the earliest of the two, the 23rd, becomes the order deadline.

records.name: Pulling the order deadline back for a new line
records.purpose: Moves an existing order's deadline earlier when a newly added line needs the goods sooner than the order was placed for.

operands.name: expected arrival of the order
operands.source: the order's header expected arrival, failing that the earliest expected arrival among the new lines
operands.constraints: the anchor of the candidate

operands.name: expected arrival of each new line
operands.source: the lines just added to the order
operands.constraints: the earliest is used when the order has no header arrival

operands.name: vendor lead time
operands.source: the vendor pricelist entry selected for the product
operands.constraints: subtracted to derive the candidate deadline

operands.name: current order deadline
operands.source: the order deadline field
operands.constraints: compared with the candidate by date part only

preconditions.condition: The order has an expected arrival, or at least one new line has one.
preconditions.otherwise: No candidate can be formed and the deadline is left as it is.

preconditions.condition: The candidate's date part is strictly earlier than the order deadline's date part.
preconditions.otherwise: The deadline is left as it is; the rule only pulls the deadline back, never pushes it forward.

procedure: Take the order's expected arrival, or, when it has none, the earliest expected arrival among the newly added lines.
Subtract the vendor lead time in days, giving the candidate deadline.
Compare the date part of the candidate with the date part of the current order deadline.
Replace the order deadline with the candidate only when the candidate's date part is strictly earlier.
records.formula: candidate = ( order.date_planned or min over the new lines of date_planned ) − vendor_lead_time days ; order.date_order = candidate when date_part( candidate ) < date_part( order.date_order )

rounding.what: Nothing: the result is a timestamp and the comparison is on date parts.
rounding.precision: Not applicable; only the date parts are compared, so the time of day is ignored by the test.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: order deadline of the existing order
result.unit_or_currency: a timestamp
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the purchase order, possibly replacing the deadline chosen when the order was created.

edge_cases.case: The candidate falls on the same calendar day as the current deadline.
edge_cases.outcome: The comparison is strict on date parts, so the deadline is not changed even when the candidate is earlier in the day.

edge_cases.case: The candidate is later than the current deadline.
edge_cases.outcome: The deadline is left as it is.

edge_cases.case: The order has no header expected arrival.
edge_cases.outcome: The earliest expected arrival among the new lines is used in its place.

edge_cases.case: The vendor has no lead time.
edge_cases.outcome: The candidate equals the expected arrival itself.

worked_examples.description: A new line needing the goods on the 25th with a seven-day lead time on an order deadlined the 21st
worked_examples.narrative: The candidate deadline is the 25th minus seven days, that is the 18th, whose date part is strictly earlier than the 21st, so the order deadline is pulled back to the 18th.

worked_examples.description: A new line needing the goods on the 30th with the same lead time
worked_examples.narrative: The candidate is the 23rd, which is not earlier than the 21st, so the deadline is left where it is.

records.name: The lead-time contribution of a buy rule
records.purpose: Gives the number of days a buy rule adds when the scheduler works out how long a replenishment takes, which is what sets the order deadline and the expected arrival of a scheduled request for quotation.

operands.name: vendor lead time
operands.source: the vendor pricelist entry selected for the product
operands.constraints: added unless the caller asks to ignore it

operands.name: days to purchase of the company
operands.source: the company setting for the time the buying process itself takes
operands.constraints: added always

operands.name: whether the product has a vendor at all
operands.source: the vendor pricelist of the product
operands.constraints: when it has none, a fixed penalty of 365 days is added

preconditions.condition: The route being evaluated contains a buy rule.
preconditions.otherwise: The buy rule contributes nothing and the delay comes from the other rules of the route.

preconditions.condition: The product has a vendor.
preconditions.otherwise: A fixed penalty of 365 days is added, with the explanation line "No Vendor Found: + 365 day(s)", where the number is the fixed penalty.

procedure: Add the vendor lead time in days to the total delay, unless the caller has asked to ignore the vendor lead time.
Add the company's days-to-purchase setting in days to the total delay.
When the product has no vendor at all, add a further 365 days.

Record the explanation lines: "Receipt Date" with the vendor lead time, "Vendor Lead Time: + n day(s)" with the number of days, "Order Deadline" with the days-to-purchase value, "Days to Purchase: + n day(s)" with the number of days, and "No Vendor Found: + 365 day(s)" when the penalty applies.
records.formula: total_delay = total_delay + vendor_lead_time ( unless the caller asks to ignore the vendor lead time ) + company.days_to_purchase + 365 when the product has no vendor at all

rounding.what: Nothing: the delay is a whole number of days.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: total delay contributed by the buy rule
result.unit_or_currency: days
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; used by the scheduler to date the request for quotation and its expected arrival.

edge_cases.case: The caller asks to ignore the vendor lead time.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the days-to-purchase value is added, plus the penalty when the product has no vendor.

edge_cases.case: The product has no vendor.
edge_cases.outcome: The penalty of 365 days is added on top of the days-to-purchase value, which makes the scheduled order visibly wrong and draws attention to the missing vendor.

edge_cases.case: The company's days-to-purchase value is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the vendor lead time is added.

edge_cases.case: Both the vendor lead time and the days-to-purchase value are zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The buy rule contributes nothing and the request for quotation is dated on the day the goods are needed.

worked_examples.description: A product needed on the 30th with a seven-day vendor lead time and two days to purchase
worked_examples.narrative: Seven days of vendor lead time plus two days to purchase is nine days, so the scheduler plans a request for quotation dated the 30th minus nine days, that is the 21st, with an expected arrival of the 28th, seven days after the deadline.

records.name: The merge tolerance on two expected arrivals
records.purpose: Decides whether two lines of two requests for quotation are close enough in time to be merged into one line.

operands.name: expected arrival of the first line
operands.source: the surviving order's line
operands.constraints: compared with the second

operands.name: expected arrival of the second line
operands.source: the absorbed order's line
operands.constraints: compared with the first

operands.name: merge tolerance
operands.source: fixed at 86 400 seconds, that is one whole day
operands.constraints: an absolute tolerance, not a precision

preconditions.condition: The two lines agree on product, unit of measure, analytic distribution and discount.
preconditions.otherwise: They are not merged, whatever their expected arrivals; the date test is the last of the four.

preconditions.condition: Both lines carry an expected arrival.
preconditions.otherwise: No comparison can be made and the lines are not merged.

procedure: Check that the two lines agree on product, on unit of measure, on analytic distribution and on discount.
Subtract one expected arrival from the other and take the absolute value of the difference in seconds.
Merge the two lines when that difference does not exceed 86 400 seconds, that is one whole day.
Leave the two lines separate otherwise, so that the survivor carries both.
records.formula: the two lines may merge when | line_a.date_planned − line_b.date_planned | ≤ 86 400 seconds

rounding.what: Nothing: the tolerance is an absolute number of seconds, not a precision.
rounding.precision: The tolerance is 86 400 seconds exactly.
rounding.method: Not applicable; the comparison uses the absolute difference and accepts a difference of exactly the tolerance.
rounding.step: At the comparison.

result.name: verdict that the two lines may merge
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, the result is a yes or no answer
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it decides whether the two lines become one.

edge_cases.case: The difference is exactly 86 400 seconds.
edge_cases.outcome: The lines merge, because the test does not exceed the tolerance rather than falls strictly below it.

edge_cases.case: The two lines differ in discount.
edge_cases.outcome: They do not merge whatever the dates, and the survivor carries both lines.

edge_cases.case: The two lines differ in unit of measure.
edge_cases.outcome: They do not merge, even for the same product.

edge_cases.case: Two orders that each belong to a different alternative group are merged.
edge_cases.outcome: The survivor's alternative set absorbs the absorbed orders' alternative sets.

worked_examples.description: Two lines fifteen hours apart
worked_examples.narrative: Fifteen hours is 54 000 seconds, which is under the 86 400-second tolerance, so the two lines merge.

worked_examples.description: The same lines twenty-five hours apart
worked_examples.narrative: Twenty-five hours is 90 000 seconds, which exceeds the tolerance, so the lines do not merge and the survivor carries both.

records.name: The merged quantity and unit price
records.purpose: Gives the quantity and the unit price the surviving line takes when two lines are merged, which is an addition on the quantity and a minimum on the price.

operands.name: total quantity of the surviving line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the line of the order that survives the merge
operands.constraints: the two lines share a unit, which is one of the merge conditions

operands.name: total quantity of the absorbed line
operands.source: the line of the order that is absorbed
operands.constraints: added to the survivor's quantity

operands.name: unit price of the surviving line
operands.unit_or_currency: the order currency per line unit
operands.source: the line of the order that survives
operands.constraints: compared with the absorbed line's price

operands.name: unit price of the absorbed line
operands.unit_or_currency: the order currency per line unit
operands.source: the line of the order that is absorbed
operands.constraints: compared with the survivor's price

preconditions.condition: The two lines satisfy the merge conditions on product, unit, analytic distribution, discount and expected arrival.
preconditions.otherwise: They are not merged and the survivor carries both lines separately.

preconditions.condition: The two orders agree on vendor, currency and destination.
preconditions.otherwise: The orders themselves are not merged and no line merge is attempted.

procedure: Add the absorbed line's total quantity to the surviving line's total quantity.
Take the smaller of the two unit prices as the surviving line's unit price, so that the merged line keeps the better of the two offers.
Leave the discount, the unit of measure, the analytic distribution and the expected arrival of the survivor unchanged, since the merge conditions required them to agree.
Recompute the surviving line's subtotal, total and tax from the merged quantity and price.
records.formula: surviving_line.product_qty = surviving_line.product_qty + incoming_line.product_qty ; surviving_line.price_unit = min( surviving_line.price_unit , incoming_line.price_unit )

rounding.what: The recomputed subtotal, total and tax of the merged line.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the order currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied by the tax engine.
rounding.step: When the merged line's amounts are recomputed, once.

result.name: merged quantity and unit price of the surviving line
result.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line, and the order currency per line unit
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the surviving purchase order line; the absorbed order's line is removed.

edge_cases.case: The absorbed line is cheaper.
edge_cases.outcome: The survivor takes the absorbed line's price, so the merge can lower the survivor's price.

edge_cases.case: The survivor is cheaper.
edge_cases.outcome: Its price is kept.

edge_cases.case: The two prices are equal.
edge_cases.outcome: The minimum is that price and nothing changes.

edge_cases.case: Merging pushes the merged quantity above what the vendor's pricelist entry covers.
edge_cases.outcome: The unit price is not recomputed from the pricelist; the minimum of the two typed prices stands.

worked_examples.description: Thirty units at 4.10 merged with twenty units at 3.95
worked_examples.narrative: The quantities add to fifty and the price is the smaller of 4.10 and 3.95, that is 3.95, so the merged line's subtotal is fifty multiplied by 3.95, that is 197.50.

records.name: The matching tolerance
records.purpose: Fixes the single absolute tolerance every total comparison of the bill-matching routine uses, and states where it may not be applied.

operands.name: tolerance
operands.source: a fixed absolute value of 0.02
operands.constraints: an absolute amount, not a precision and not a percentage

operands.name: total being compared
operands.source: the total of the incoming bill, or a summed remaining amount of order lines
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

preconditions.condition: The comparison is between two totals.
preconditions.otherwise: The tolerance is not applied at all: a unit price comparison in the pairing branch requires exact equality.

preconditions.condition: Both totals are expressed in the bill's currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The comparison is meaningless; the tolerance is an absolute amount in that currency and not a relative one.

procedure: Take the fixed tolerance of 0.02, expressed in the bill's currency.
Apply it as a symmetric band around the target total, from the target minus the tolerance to the target plus the tolerance.
Apply it only to totals; never apply it to a unit price, which is compared for exact equality.
records.formula: TOLERANCE = 0.02 , expressed in the bill's currency and applied to totals only

rounding.what: Nothing: the tolerance is a fixed absolute amount.
rounding.precision: 0.02 in the bill's currency.
rounding.method: Not applicable; it is a band, not a rounding.
rounding.step: At every total comparison of the matching routine.

result.name: matching tolerance
result.unit_or_currency: the currency of the bill
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; a fixed value used by the total match test, the vendor-and-amount fallback and the subset search.

edge_cases.case: A currency whose rounding step is coarser than 0.02.
edge_cases.outcome: The tolerance is still 0.02 in that currency, so it can be narrower than one rounding step; the domain does not scale it to the currency.

edge_cases.case: A difference of exactly 0.02.
edge_cases.outcome: The total match test is strict on both sides, so a difference of exactly the tolerance does not match.

edge_cases.case: A unit price comparison.
edge_cases.outcome: The tolerance is not applied; the pairing branch requires an exact equality of unit prices.

worked_examples.description: The band around a bill total of five hundred and one hundredth
worked_examples.narrative: The band runs from 500.01 minus 0.02, that is 499.99, to 500.01 plus 0.02, that is 500.03.

records.name: The remaining amount of an order line
records.purpose: Gives the part of a line's total including tax that has not yet been billed, which is the figure the matching routine adds up and compares with an incoming bill's total.

operands.name: billed quantity of the line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the computed billed quantity
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: ordered quantity of the line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the total quantity field of the order line
operands.constraints: strictly non-zero, because only lines with a non-zero ordered quantity are considered

operands.name: total including tax of the line
operands.source: the computed line total
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

preconditions.condition: The line's ordered quantity is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The line is not considered at all, which is what makes the division safe.

preconditions.condition: The line belongs to a candidate order.
preconditions.otherwise: It is not part of the comparison.

procedure: Divide the billed quantity by the ordered quantity, giving the fraction of the line already billed.
Subtract that fraction from one, giving the fraction still to bill.
Multiply the line's total including tax by the fraction still to bill.
Use the product as the line's remaining amount in every comparison of the matching routine.
records.formula: amount_to_invoice( line ) = ( 1 − qty_invoiced ÷ product_qty ) × price_total

rounding.what: The remaining amount when it is compared.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the bill's currency, together with the absolute tolerance of 0.02.
rounding.step: At the comparison; the fraction itself is not rounded.

result.name: remaining amount of the line
result.unit_or_currency: the order currency, compared against the bill's currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; computed each time the matching routine runs.

edge_cases.case: Nothing has been billed.
edge_cases.outcome: The fraction still to bill is one and the remaining amount is the whole line total including tax.

edge_cases.case: The line is fully billed.
edge_cases.outcome: The fraction is zero and the remaining amount is zero, so the line contributes nothing to the comparison.

edge_cases.case: More has been billed than was ordered.
edge_cases.outcome: The fraction is negative and the remaining amount is negative, which lowers the summed target.

edge_cases.case: A line with a zero ordered quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: It is excluded from the comparison entirely, so the division by the ordered quantity is always safe.

worked_examples.description: A line of ten units totalling 600.00 including tax, four of them billed
worked_examples.narrative: Four of ten is a billed fraction of 0.4, so the remaining fraction is 0.6 and the remaining amount is 600.00 multiplied by 0.6, that is 360.00.

records.name: The total match test
records.purpose: Decides whether an incoming bill's total agrees with the summed remaining amounts of an order's lines, which is the first branch of the matching routine.

operands.name: total of the incoming bill
operands.source: the bill being matched
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: remaining amount of each line of the candidate order
operands.source: the computed remaining amounts
operands.constraints: summed into one figure

operands.name: tolerance
operands.source: the fixed matching tolerance of 0.02
operands.constraints: applied as a symmetric band

preconditions.condition: The candidate order has at least one line with a non-zero ordered quantity.
preconditions.otherwise: No remaining amount can be summed and the test fails.

preconditions.condition: The bill and the order are expressed in the same currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The comparison is not meaningful; the matching routine works within one currency.

procedure: Sum the remaining amounts of the candidate order's lines.
Form the band around the bill's total: from the total minus the tolerance to the total plus the tolerance.
Report a match when the summed remaining amount lies strictly inside that band, that is strictly above the lower bound and strictly below the upper bound.
Report no match otherwise, and let the routine fall through to the next branch.
records.formula: total_match holds exactly when amount_total − TOLERANCE < Σ amount_to_invoice( line ) < amount_total + TOLERANCE

rounding.what: Both sides of the comparison.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the bill's currency, with the absolute tolerance of 0.02 applied on top.
rounding.method: Half away from zero for the amounts; the tolerance is a band, not a rounding.
rounding.step: At the comparison.

result.name: verdict that the bill matches the order in total
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable, the result is a yes or no answer
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it decides whether every line of the order is proposed with its full quantity.

edge_cases.case: The summed remaining amount equals the bill total exactly.
edge_cases.outcome: It lies strictly inside the band and the test matches.

edge_cases.case: The difference is exactly the tolerance.
edge_cases.outcome: The comparison is strict on both sides, so the test does not match.

edge_cases.case: The order is fully billed already.
edge_cases.outcome: Every remaining amount is zero, the sum is zero, and the test matches only a bill whose total is within the tolerance of zero.

edge_cases.case: The bill total is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The band is formed around the negative total and the comparison proceeds unchanged.

worked_examples.description: A bill of 900.00 against an order with 900.00 still to bill
worked_examples.narrative: The summed remaining amount of 900.00 lies strictly between 899.98 and 900.02, so the bill matches the order in total.

worked_examples.description: A bill of 900.00 against an order with 900.02 still to bill
worked_examples.narrative: The summed remaining amount equals the upper bound and the comparison is strict, so the test does not match and the routine falls through.

records.name: The vendor-and-amount fallback
records.purpose: Finds an order for an incoming bill when no reference identifies one, by looking for a single order of the same vendor whose total is within the tolerance of the bill's.

operands.name: total of the incoming bill
operands.source: the bill being matched
operands.constraints: the centre of the band

operands.name: vendor of the bill
operands.source: the partner of the bill
operands.constraints: an order of any of the vendor's children also qualifies

operands.name: total of each candidate order
operands.source: the purchase orders of that vendor
operands.constraints: must lie inside the band

operands.name: status of each candidate order
operands.source: the status field, whose confirmed value is `purchase`
operands.constraints: only confirmed orders qualify

operands.name: billing status of each candidate order
operands.source: the billing status field, whose qualifying stored values are `to invoice` (something still to bill) and `no` (nothing to bill)
operands.constraints: an order already fully billed does not qualify

operands.name: tolerance
operands.source: the fixed matching tolerance of 0.02
operands.constraints: applied as a symmetric band

preconditions.condition: No earlier branch of the matching routine has already identified an order.
preconditions.otherwise: The fallback is not attempted.

preconditions.condition: Exactly one candidate is found.
preconditions.otherwise: The fallback does not fire at all: with none there is nothing to match, and with more than one the choice would be ambiguous.

procedure: Select the purchase orders whose vendor is the bill's vendor, or any of that vendor's children.
Keep those whose status is the confirmed status.
Keep those whose billing status is the something-still-to-bill status or the nothing-to-bill status.
Keep those whose total lies between the bill's total minus the tolerance and the bill's total plus the tolerance.
Fire the fallback only when exactly one candidate remains, and match the bill to that order.
records.formula: candidates = the orders of this vendor or of any of its children whose status is `purchase` , whose billing status is in { `to invoice` , `no` } , and whose amount_total lies between amount_total_of_bill − TOLERANCE and amount_total_of_bill + TOLERANCE ; the fallback fires only when exactly one candidate is found

rounding.what: The order totals against the band.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the bill's currency, with the absolute tolerance of 0.02 applied on top.
rounding.method: Half away from zero for the amounts.
rounding.step: At the selection of the candidates.

result.name: the single matched order, or no match
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored as a figure; the bill's lines are linked to that order's lines.

edge_cases.case: Two orders of the same vendor have the same total.
edge_cases.outcome: Two candidates are found, the fallback does not fire, and the bill keeps its own lines.

edge_cases.case: No order of the vendor has a total within the tolerance.
edge_cases.outcome: No candidate is found and the fallback does not fire.

edge_cases.case: The vendor is a child contact of the ordering company.
edge_cases.outcome: Orders of the parent and of its children are all considered, so a bill addressed by a subsidiary can still find the parent's order.

edge_cases.case: An order is already fully billed.
edge_cases.outcome: Its billing status is the invoiced status, which is not among the two qualifying values, so it is excluded.

worked_examples.description: One order of the vendor within the tolerance of a bill of 1 200.00
worked_examples.narrative: Only order A's total of 1 200.01 lies inside the band from 1 199.98 to 1 200.02, so exactly one candidate is found and the fallback matches the bill to it.

records.name: The subset search over remaining amounts
records.purpose: Finds the unique subset of an order's lines whose remaining amounts add up to the incoming bill's total, and abandons the search when the subset is not unique.

operands.name: remaining amount of each line of the order
operands.source: the computed remaining amounts
operands.constraints: sorted descending before the search begins

operands.name: target total
operands.source: the bill's total at the top level, and the target reduced by the chosen line at each recursion
operands.constraints: may fall below zero as the recursion proceeds

operands.name: tolerance
operands.source: the fixed matching tolerance of 0.02
operands.constraints: applied as a symmetric band at each position

preconditions.condition: The lines are sorted by remaining amount descending before the search begins.
preconditions.otherwise: The recursion explores the same combinations in a different order and can record a different first solution, so the sort is part of the specification.

preconditions.condition: The search completes inside its time budget.
preconditions.otherwise: It abandons, writes a warning to the technical log and reports no match.

procedure: Sort the lines by remaining amount, largest first.
At position one, with the bill total as the target, and at each later position with the reduced target, do the following.

When the line's remaining amount is strictly below the target minus the tolerance, recurse over the lines after it with the target reduced by that remaining amount, and prepend the line to every solution the recursion returns.
Otherwise, when the line's remaining amount lies within the tolerance band around the target, record the single-line solution consisting of that line.
As soon as more than one solution has been recorded at a level, abandon the search and return nothing, so that an ambiguous total never silently picks the wrong lines.
Return the unique solution when exactly one has been recorded.
records.formula: at position i with the remaining target g : if amount_to_invoice( line_i ) < g − TOLERANCE then recurse over the lines after i with target g − amount_to_invoice( line_i ) and prepend line_i to every solution found ; else if g − TOLERANCE ≤ amount_to_invoice( line_i ) ≤ g + TOLERANCE then record the single-line solution [ line_i ] ; if more than one solution has been recorded at this level then abandon and return nothing

rounding.what: Each remaining amount and each target against the band.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the bill's currency, with the absolute tolerance of 0.02 applied on top.
rounding.method: Half away from zero for the amounts; the tolerance is a band, not a rounding.
rounding.step: At each comparison inside the recursion.

result.name: the unique subset of lines, or no match
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored as a figure; the bill's lines are paired with the lines of the returned subset, or the bill falls through to the order-match branch.

edge_cases.case: Two solutions are found.
edge_cases.outcome: The search abandons and reports no match; the bill falls through to the order-match branch and every line of the order is proposed with its full quantity.

edge_cases.case: No subset adds up to the target.
edge_cases.outcome: The search returns nothing and the routine falls through.

edge_cases.case: The search exceeds its time budget.
edge_cases.outcome: It abandons, writes a warning to the technical log and reports no match.

edge_cases.case: A line's remaining amount is exactly the target.
edge_cases.outcome: It falls inside the band and is recorded as a single-line solution rather than being recursed past.

edge_cases.case: A line's remaining amount exceeds the upper bound of the band.
edge_cases.outcome: Neither branch applies, so the line is skipped at that position and the search continues with the next line.

worked_examples.description: Four lines and a bill total that two different subsets match
worked_examples.narrative: At position one, 500.00 is not below 499.99 and lies inside the band from 499.99 to 500.03, so the single-line solution of 500.00 is recorded. At position two, 300.00 is below 499.99, so the search recurses with a target of 200.01 over 200.00 and 120.00, where 200.00 lies inside the band from 199.99 to 200.03 and the solution of 300.00 with 200.00 is also recorded. Two solutions now exist, so the search abandons and returns nothing, and the bill falls through to the order-match branch.

worked_examples.description: The same four lines against a total that only one subset matches
worked_examples.narrative: Only the pair of 500.00 and 120.00 adds to within the tolerance of 620.01, so exactly one solution is recorded and that unique subset is returned.

records.name: The line pairing similarity
records.purpose: Chooses which order line an incoming bill line is paired with, by an exact price test first and a textual similarity as the tie-break.

operands.name: unit price of the bill line
operands.source: the bill line being paired
operands.constraints: compared for exact equality, with no tolerance at all

operands.name: unit price of the candidate order line
operands.source: the order line being considered
operands.constraints: compared for exact equality

operands.name: quantity of the bill line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the bill line
operands.source: the bill line being paired
operands.constraints: must not exceed the candidate's remaining quantity

operands.name: ordered quantity and billed quantity of the candidate order line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the order line
operands.source: the order line
operands.constraints: their difference is the candidate's remaining quantity

operands.name: label of the bill line and description of the order line
operands.source: the two records
operands.constraints: compared by a textual similarity ratio between 0 and 1, where 1 means identical

preconditions.condition: At least one candidate order line has exactly the bill line's unit price.
preconditions.otherwise: No pairing is made for that bill line; it stays unmatched, and when exactly one bill is involved the surplus order lines are appended to it as new lines.

preconditions.condition: The bill line's quantity does not exceed the candidate's remaining quantity.
preconditions.otherwise: The candidate is rejected, whatever the similarity of the labels.

procedure: Select the candidate order lines whose unit price equals the bill line's unit price exactly, with no tolerance.
Among those, keep the candidates whose remaining quantity, that is the ordered quantity minus the billed quantity, is not below the bill line's quantity.
Compute the textual similarity ratio between the bill line's label and each remaining candidate's description, a number between zero and one where one means identical.
Pair the bill line with the candidate whose similarity is the highest.
records.formula: candidate holds exactly when invoice_line.price_unit = purchase_line.price_unit and invoice_line.quantity ≤ purchase_line.product_qty − purchase_line.qty_invoiced ; the winner is the candidate with the highest textual similarity ratio between the bill line's label and the order line's description

rounding.what: Nothing: the price test is an exact equality and the similarity is a ratio between zero and one.
rounding.precision: Not applicable; the unit price comparison is the single exact test of the domain and carries no tolerance.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the paired order line, or none
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored as a figure; the bill line is linked to the chosen order line, which changes that line's billed quantity.

edge_cases.case: Two candidates have the same unit price and the same similarity.
edge_cases.outcome: One of them is chosen; the similarity only breaks the tie and does not guarantee a unique winner when the labels are equally close.

edge_cases.case: More bill lines than order lines exist for a product.
edge_cases.outcome: The surplus bill lines are all attached to the last order line of that product.

edge_cases.case: More order lines than bill lines exist for a product.
edge_cases.outcome: The surplus order lines stay unmatched and, when exactly one bill is involved, are appended to it as new lines.

edge_cases.case: More than one bill is involved in the match.
edge_cases.outcome: Unmatched bill lines are not deleted and unmatched order lines are not appended; only the pairings are written.

edge_cases.case: The unit prices differ by one hundredth.
edge_cases.outcome: No candidate is found, because the price test is exact and the matching tolerance is never applied to a unit price.

worked_examples.description: One bill line against two order lines at the same price
worked_examples.narrative: Both order lines have the exact unit price of 60.00 and enough remaining quantity, so both are candidates; the similarity of the labels is one for the first and much lower for the second, so the bill line is paired with the first.

records.name: The valuation unit price at billing time
records.purpose: Gives the standard cost restated into the bill line's unit and currency, which is the figure the billed price is compared with to find a price difference.

operands.name: standard cost of the product
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of the product
operands.source: the cost field of the product under the standard-price cost method
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: reference unit of measure of the product and unit of measure of the bill line
operands.source: the product and the bill line
operands.constraints: must belong to the same category

operands.name: company currency and bill currency
operands.source: the company of the bill and the bill itself
operands.constraints: the conversion is made without rounding

operands.name: company of the bill
operands.source: the bill
operands.constraints: its rate table is consulted

operands.name: date of the bill line
