operands.source: the bill line
operands.constraints: the conversion date

operands.name: document type of the bill
operands.source: the bill
operands.constraints: a vendor refund negates the valuation price

preconditions.condition: Inventory valuation is installed and the company uses the recognition style in which stock is debited at bill time.
preconditions.otherwise: No price difference is computed at all and no valuation price is needed.

preconditions.condition: The product's cost method is the standard-price method.
preconditions.otherwise: The price difference does not apply; it is computed only for products valued at a standard price.

procedure: Take the product's standard cost, which is expressed per reference unit of the product in the company currency.
Convert it from the product reference unit into the bill line's unit of measure, using the price conversion.
Convert the result from the company currency into the bill currency, for the bill's company, at the bill line's date, without rounding.
Negate the result when the document is a vendor refund, which reverses the sign of the whole adjustment.
records.formula: valuation_price_unit = convert( convert_price( product.standard_price , product_reference_unit , bill_line_unit ) , from = company_currency , to = bill_currency , company = bill_company , date = bill_line_date , round = false ) , negated when the document is a vendor refund

rounding.what: Nothing at this step: the currency conversion is performed with rounding disabled.
rounding.precision: Not applicable here; the Product Price precision is used later, by the comparison that decides whether the adjustment is produced.
rounding.step: None; the rounding belongs to the journal items the adjustment produces.

result.name: valuation unit price of the bill line
result.unit_or_currency: the bill currency per unit of the bill line
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; subtracted from the gross unit price to give the price difference per unit.

edge_cases.case: The bill currency equals the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The currency conversion is a no-op and only the unit restatement applies.

edge_cases.case: The bill line's unit is the product reference unit.
edge_cases.outcome: The unit restatement is a no-op.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor refund.
edge_cases.outcome: The valuation price is negated before the subtraction, which reverses the sign of the whole adjustment.

edge_cases.case: The product's standard cost is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The valuation price is zero and the whole billed price becomes a price difference.

edge_cases.case: The product's cost method is not the standard-price method.
edge_cases.outcome: No valuation price is computed and no price difference is produced.

worked_examples.description: A standard cost of nine in the company currency, billed in the same currency per reference unit
worked_examples.narrative: Neither the unit restatement nor the currency conversion changes the figure, so the valuation price is 9.00 per unit.

records.name: The price difference per unit and its subtotal
records.purpose: Gives the amount by which the billed price exceeds the standard cost, and the two conditions under which the balancing journal items are produced.

operands.name: gross unit price of the bill line
operands.unit_or_currency: the bill currency per unit of the bill line
operands.source: the four-step gross unit price computed for the bill line
operands.constraints: the billed price after the discount and after the taxes are removed

operands.name: valuation unit price
operands.unit_or_currency: the bill currency per unit of the bill line
operands.source: the standard cost restated into the bill line's unit and currency
operands.constraints: negated for a vendor refund

operands.name: quantity of the bill line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the bill line
operands.source: the bill line
operands.constraints: the relevant quantity of the subtotal

operands.name: stored unit price of the bill line and its recomputed unit price
operands.source: the bill line
operands.constraints: compared at the Product Price precision

preconditions.condition: The subtotal is not zero in the bill's currency.
preconditions.otherwise: No balancing journal item is produced, because there is nothing to correct.

preconditions.condition: The line's stored unit price still equals its computed unit price at the Product Price precision.
preconditions.otherwise: The adjustment is suppressed; a discount that has been applied makes the two differ, and the comparison then suppresses the adjustment.

preconditions.condition: A price-difference account is resolvable for the product's category.
preconditions.otherwise: No adjustment can be posted.

procedure: Subtract the valuation unit price from the gross unit price, giving the price difference per unit.
Multiply the price difference per unit by the bill line's quantity, giving the subtotal.
Test that the subtotal is not zero at the bill currency's rounding.
Test that the line's stored unit price still equals its computed unit price at the Product Price precision.
Produce the two balancing journal items only when both tests pass.
records.formula: price_unit_val_dif = gross_unit_price − valuation_price_unit ; price_subtotal = bill_line_quantity × price_unit_val_dif

rounding.what: The subtotal, when it is compared with zero and when the journal items are written.
rounding.precision: The rounding of the bill currency for the zero test, and the Product Price precision for the unit price comparison.
rounding.step: At the two tests, and again when the journal item amounts are converted into the company currency.

result.name: price difference per unit and its subtotal
result.unit_or_currency: the bill currency per unit, and the bill currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored on the bill line; they become the amounts of the two balancing journal items.

edge_cases.case: A discount has been applied to the line.
edge_cases.outcome: The stored and computed unit prices differ at the Product Price precision and the adjustment is suppressed.

edge_cases.case: The billed price equals the standard cost.
edge_cases.outcome: The subtotal is zero at the bill currency's rounding and no journal item is produced.

edge_cases.case: The billed price is below the standard cost.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is negative and the two journal items swap sides: the price-difference account is credited and the line's own account debited.

edge_cases.case: The document is a vendor refund.
edge_cases.outcome: The valuation price was negated, which reverses the sign of the whole adjustment.

edge_cases.case: The unit price of the line is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The whole standard cost becomes a price difference.

worked_examples.description: Ten units billed at ten against a standard cost of nine
worked_examples.narrative: The difference per unit is 10.00 minus 9.00, that is 1.00, and the subtotal is ten multiplied by 1.00, that is 10.00; the subtotal is not zero and the prices agree, so the two balancing items are produced and ten units' worth of extra cost is moved out of the stock account and into the price-difference account.

records.name: The two balancing journal items of the price difference
records.purpose: Gives the amounts, sides and accounts of the two journal items the price difference produces, which is what corrects the stock account to the standard cost.

operands.name: price difference per unit
operands.unit_or_currency: the bill currency per unit of the bill line
operands.source: the computed difference between the gross unit price and the valuation price
operands.constraints: may be positive or negative

operands.name: quantity of the bill line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the bill line
operands.source: the bill line
operands.constraints: the quantity both items carry

operands.name: price-difference account of the product's category
operands.source: the product category, mapped through the bill's fiscal position
operands.constraints: must be resolvable for the adjustment to be produced

operands.name: account of the bill line
operands.source: the bill line
operands.constraints: the account the second item corrects

operands.name: company currency and bill currency
operands.source: the company of the bill and the bill
operands.constraints: the conversion uses today's date, not the bill's date

preconditions.condition: Both eligibility tests of the price difference passed.
preconditions.otherwise: No item is produced at all.

preconditions.condition: A price-difference account is resolvable on the product's category and mapped through the bill's fiscal position.
preconditions.otherwise: No item is produced.

procedure: Compute the amount as the bill line's quantity multiplied by the price difference per unit, converted into the company currency; the conversion uses today's date, not the bill's date.
Post the first item to the category's price-difference account, mapped through the bill's fiscal position, as a debit when the difference is positive.
Post the second item to the bill line's own account, as a credit when the difference is positive, for the same amount with the opposite sign.

Give both items the first sixty-four characters of the bill line's label; the line's partner, or the bill's commercial partner; the product and unit copied from the line; the bill line's quantity; the line's analytic distribution; no taxes; and a display role that marks them as cost-recognition items rather than ordinary product lines.
records.formula: price difference item = convert_to_company_currency( bill_line_quantity × price_unit_val_dif ) , debited when the difference is positive ; correction item = convert_to_company_currency( bill_line_quantity × ( − price_unit_val_dif ) ) , credited when the difference is positive

rounding.what: The two journal item amounts.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: Once, when each item's amount is written; the conversion into the company currency uses today's date.

result.name: the two balancing journal items
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Written as journal items of the vendor bill's journal entry, alongside the ordinary product, tax and payable items.

edge_cases.case: The difference is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The two sides swap: the price-difference account is credited and the bill line's own account debited.

edge_cases.case: The bill line's label is longer than sixty-four characters.
edge_cases.outcome: It is truncated to the first sixty-four for both items.

edge_cases.case: The bill line has no partner.
edge_cases.outcome: The bill's commercial partner is used on both items.

edge_cases.case: The bill line carries an analytic distribution.
edge_cases.outcome: Both items carry the same distribution.

edge_cases.case: The conversion rate has changed between the bill's date and today.
edge_cases.outcome: Today's rate is used, so the two items can be converted at a different rate from the ordinary product line of the same bill; this is the behaviour as observed and a rebuild must reproduce it to post the same entry.

worked_examples.description: Ten units billed at ten against a standard cost of nine, in the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: The bill's own product line has already debited the stock input account with 100.00; the price-difference item debits 10.00 to the price-difference account and the correction item credits 10.00 to the stock input account, so the stock input account is relieved by only 90.00 net, which is the standard cost, and the 10.00 excess lands in the price-difference account.

records.name: The billed quantity and billed value of a purchase line
records.purpose: Accumulates, over the posted bills of a purchase line, the quantity billed and the money value billed, which is what inventory values an incoming movement from when any bill exists.

operands.name: quantity of each bill line of the purchase line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the bill line
operands.source: the bill lines linked to the purchase order line
operands.constraints: converted into the product reference unit before it is added

operands.name: subtotal of each bill line
operands.source: the bill line
operands.constraints: divided by the bill line's currency rate and rounded to the currency

operands.name: currency rate of each bill line
operands.source: the bill holding the line
operands.constraints: strictly positive

operands.name: date of each bill line
operands.source: the bill line
operands.constraints: a line dated after the requested date is skipped

operands.name: status of each bill
operands.source: the bill holding the line
operands.constraints: a bill that is not posted is skipped

operands.name: document type of each bill
operands.source: the bill holding the line
operands.constraints: a vendor bill adds and a vendor refund subtracts

preconditions.condition: At least one posted bill line exists that is dated on or before the requested date.
preconditions.otherwise: The billed quantity is not positive and the movement falls back to the generic valuation.

preconditions.condition: The requested date is known.
preconditions.otherwise: Every bill line of the purchase line is walked, with no date restriction.

procedure: Walk the bill lines of the purchase line.
Skip a bill line dated after the requested date, and skip one whose document is not posted.

For a vendor bill, add the bill line's quantity converted into the product reference unit to the billed quantity, and add its subtotal divided by its currency rate, rounded to the currency, to the billed value.
For a vendor refund, subtract both figures instead.
When the accumulated billed quantity is not positive, abandon the bill-based valuation and fall back to the generic valuation.
records.formula: billed_quantity = billed_quantity + convert_quantity( bill_line.quantity , bill_line.unit , product_reference_unit ) ; billed_value = billed_value + round_to_currency( bill_line.price_subtotal ÷ bill_line.currency_rate ) ; both added for a vendor bill and subtracted for a vendor refund

rounding.what: Each bill line's contribution to the billed value, before it is added.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency for the value, and the rounding of the product reference unit for the quantity.
rounding.step: Once per bill line, on the value after the division by the currency rate; the accumulated total is not rounded again.

result.name: billed quantity and billed value of the purchase line
result.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product, and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the apportionment that values the goods movement.

edge_cases.case: Every bill of the line is a draft.
edge_cases.outcome: No line is counted, the billed quantity is zero, and the movement falls back to the generic valuation.

edge_cases.case: The refunds exceed the bills.
edge_cases.outcome: The billed quantity is negative, which is not positive, so the movement falls back to the generic valuation.

edge_cases.case: A bill line is dated after the requested date.
edge_cases.outcome: It is skipped, so a valuation asked for at a past date does not see later bills.

edge_cases.case: A bill line is expressed in a unit other than the product reference unit.
edge_cases.outcome: Its quantity is converted before it is added.

edge_cases.case: The bill is in a foreign currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The subtotal is divided by the bill line's own currency rate before it is rounded, which brings it into the company currency.

worked_examples.description: One posted bill covering ten units for six hundred at a rate of one
worked_examples.narrative: The bill line adds ten units to the billed quantity and 600.00 divided by a rate of one, that is 600.00, to the billed value.

records.name: The quantity earlier movements have already consumed
records.purpose: Gives how much of a line's billed quantity earlier goods movements have already taken, so that two movements of the same line do not both claim the same billed value.

operands.name: valued quantity of each earlier movement of the same line and product
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
operands.source: the goods movements of the same purchase line and product, dated before the movement being valued
operands.constraints: ties in date are broken by identifier

operands.name: direction of each such movement
operands.source: the goods movement
operands.constraints: an incoming or drop-shipped movement counts positively and an outgoing movement counts negatively

preconditions.condition: The movements are ordered by date, with ties broken by identifier.
preconditions.otherwise: Two movements of the same date could each see the other as earlier, and the same billed value would be claimed twice.

preconditions.condition: At least one earlier movement exists.
preconditions.otherwise: The consumed quantity is zero and the whole billed quantity is available to the movement being valued.

procedure: Select the goods movements of the same purchase line and the same product that are dated before the movement being valued, breaking a tie in date by identifier.
Add the valued quantity of each incoming or drop-shipped movement.
Subtract the valued quantity of each outgoing movement.
Use the total as the quantity already consumed from the line's billed quantity.
records.formula: other_candidates_qty = Σ over the movements of the same line and product , dated before this movement with ties broken by identifier , of ( + the valued quantity for an incoming or drop-shipped movement , − the valued quantity for an outgoing movement )

rounding.what: Nothing at this step; the quantities are already expressed in the product reference unit.
rounding.precision: The rounding of the product reference unit.
rounding.step: At the conversion of each movement's valued quantity, before it is signed and added.

result.name: quantity already consumed from the billed quantity
result.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; subtracted from the billed quantity and used to scale the billed value.

edge_cases.case: The movement being valued is the first of its line.
edge_cases.outcome: No earlier movement exists and the consumed quantity is zero.

edge_cases.case: An outgoing movement of the same line exists.
edge_cases.outcome: It reduces the consumed quantity, so the billed value it had taken becomes available again.

edge_cases.case: Two movements share a date.
edge_cases.outcome: The tie is broken by identifier, so the ordering is deterministic and the same movement is always the earlier one.

edge_cases.case: The consumed quantity reaches or exceeds the billed quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The movement falls back to the generic valuation, because there is no billed value left for it.

worked_examples.description: A second movement of four units after a first of six
worked_examples.narrative: The single earlier movement is incoming and valued at six units, so six of the line's billed quantity has already been consumed.

records.name: The reduction of the billed value by the consumed quantity
records.purpose: Scales the billed value down in proportion to what earlier movements have already taken, leaving the value that is still available to the movement being valued.

operands.name: billed quantity of the purchase line
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
operands.source: the accumulated billed quantity
operands.constraints: strictly positive, or the movement falls back to the generic valuation

operands.name: billed value of the purchase line
operands.source: the accumulated billed value
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: quantity already consumed by earlier movements
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
operands.source: the computed consumed quantity
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

preconditions.condition: The billed quantity strictly exceeds the consumed quantity.
preconditions.otherwise: The movement falls back to the generic valuation, because there is no billed value left to attribute to it.

preconditions.condition: The billed quantity is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The scaling factor is undefined; a billed quantity that is not positive has already sent the computation to the generic valuation.

procedure: Subtract the consumed quantity from the billed quantity, giving the quantity still available.
Divide the quantity still available by the billed quantity, giving the fraction of the billed value that is still available.
Multiply the billed value by that fraction, giving the remaining billed value.
Replace the billed quantity by the quantity still available, so that the apportionment that follows works on the reduced pair.
records.formula: billed_value = billed_value × ( ( billed_quantity − other_candidates_qty ) ÷ billed_quantity ) ; billed_quantity = billed_quantity − other_candidates_qty

rounding.what: The reduced billed value when it is written into the valuation.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: Once, when the resulting value is written; the fraction itself is not rounded.

result.name: remaining billed value and remaining billed quantity
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency, and the reference unit of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the apportionment that gives the movement its value.

edge_cases.case: No earlier movement exists.
edge_cases.outcome: The consumed quantity is zero, the fraction is one, and both figures pass through unchanged.

edge_cases.case: The consumed quantity equals the billed quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The billed quantity does not strictly exceed it, so the movement falls back to the generic valuation instead of taking a value of zero.

edge_cases.case: The consumed quantity is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The fraction exceeds one and the remaining billed value is larger than the accumulated one, which is what an outgoing movement of the same line restores.

edge_cases.case: The billed value is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The scaling preserves the sign.

worked_examples.description: Six of ten billed units already consumed
worked_examples.narrative: Ten minus six leaves four still available, that is a fraction of 0.4 of the billed quantity, so the remaining billed value is 600.00 multiplied by 0.4, that is 240.00 for a remaining quantity of four.

records.name: The value returned for the requested quantity
records.purpose: Gives the final answer inventory receives when it asks a purchase-linked movement what a quantity is worth, apportioning the remaining billed value when the request is smaller than what is available.

operands.name: requested quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
operands.source: the quantity inventory is asking the value of
operands.constraints: may be smaller than, equal to or larger than the remaining billed quantity

operands.name: remaining billed quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
operands.source: the billed quantity after the reduction by the consumed quantity
operands.constraints: strictly positive at this point

operands.name: remaining billed value
operands.source: the billed value after the reduction by the consumed quantity
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

preconditions.condition: The remaining billed quantity is strictly positive.
preconditions.otherwise: The movement has already fallen back to the generic valuation and this apportionment is not reached.

preconditions.condition: The requested quantity is known.
preconditions.otherwise: The movement's own completed quantity, converted into the product reference unit, is used in its place.

procedure: Compare the requested quantity with the remaining billed quantity.
When the requested quantity is not below the remaining billed quantity, return the whole remaining billed value together with the remaining billed quantity, because the bills cover no more than that.
Otherwise return the remaining billed value multiplied by the requested quantity and divided by the remaining billed quantity, together with the requested quantity.
Hand the pair of value and quantity to inventory as the movement's valuation.
records.formula: if requested_quantity ≥ billed_quantity then value = billed_value and quantity = billed_quantity ; else value = requested_quantity × billed_value ÷ billed_quantity and quantity = requested_quantity

rounding.what: The returned value.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: Once, when the value is written onto the valuation; the apportioning division is not rounded.

result.name: value and quantity of the movement's valuation
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency, and the reference unit of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: Written onto the valuation of the goods movement, with a description carrying the formatted value for the quantity, the unit name and the bill numbers.

edge_cases.case: The requested quantity exactly equals the remaining billed quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The whole remaining billed value is returned, because the test is not below rather than strictly above.

edge_cases.case: The requested quantity exceeds the remaining billed quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the remaining billed value is returned, together with the smaller billed quantity; the excess quantity is valued by the generic valuation.

edge_cases.case: The requested quantity is a fraction of the remaining billed quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The value is apportioned in proportion to the quantity.

edge_cases.case: No bill exists at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The movement is valued from the order instead, at the movement unit price multiplied by the quantity, capped at the movement's own completed quantity converted into the product reference unit, and the description says the value comes from the order name and is not billed.

worked_examples.description: Two movements of six and four against one bill of ten units for six hundred
worked_examples.narrative: The first movement asks for six of a billed quantity of ten with a billed value of 600.00 and no earlier movement, so the requested six is below ten and the value is six multiplied by 600.00 divided by ten, that is 360.00. The second movement asks for four: the earlier movement has already consumed six, so the remaining billed value is 600.00 multiplied by four divided by ten, that is 240.00, for a remaining quantity of four; the requested four is not below four, so the whole 240.00 is returned.

records.name: Valuing a movement from the order when no bill exists
records.purpose: Gives the fallback valuation of a purchase-linked movement when the bills give nothing to work from, which values the goods at the price the order was placed at.

operands.name: unit price handed to the goods movement
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit of the product
operands.source: the computed movement unit price of the purchase order line
operands.constraints: already rounded to the Product Price precision

operands.name: requested quantity
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
operands.source: the quantity inventory is asking the value of
operands.constraints: may exceed the movement's own completed quantity

operands.name: completed quantity of the movement
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the movement
operands.source: the goods movement
operands.constraints: converted into the product reference unit and used as the cap

preconditions.condition: No posted bill line of the purchase line is dated on or before the requested date, or the billed quantity is not positive, or the billed quantity does not exceed what earlier movements have consumed.
preconditions.otherwise: The bill-based valuation applies instead and this fallback is not reached.

preconditions.condition: The movement has a completed quantity.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nothing to cap and nothing to value.

procedure: Take the unit price the order handed to the goods movement.
Multiply it by the requested quantity.
Cap the quantity at the movement's own completed quantity, converted into the product reference unit, so that the valuation never covers more than the movement itself carries.
Record the valuation with a description carrying the formatted value for the quantity, the unit name and the order name, and stating that the value is not billed.
records.formula: value = move_price_unit × min( requested_quantity , completed quantity of the movement converted into the product reference unit )

rounding.what: The resulting value.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency; the unit price was already rounded to the Product Price precision when it was handed to the movement.
rounding.step: Once, when the value is written onto the valuation.

result.name: value of the movement's valuation
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Written onto the valuation of the goods movement, with a description that names the order and states that the value is not billed.

edge_cases.case: The requested quantity exceeds the movement's completed quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The cap applies and only the completed quantity is valued.

edge_cases.case: The order's unit price is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The valuation is zero, and the whole standard cost becomes a price difference when the bill later arrives.

edge_cases.case: A bill arrives later.
edge_cases.outcome: The movement is re-valued from the bills, and the correction is attributed to the earliest unconsumed portion of the billed quantity.

edge_cases.case: The order line's unit price is changed on a confirmed order.
edge_cases.outcome: The open movements of that line have their unit price rewritten and the already valued movements are re-valued.

worked_examples.description: Six units valued at the order's movement unit price of 7.60
worked_examples.narrative: Six units at 7.60 each is 45.60, and the cap does not bite because the requested quantity equals the movement's own completed quantity.

records.name: The delay and the delay to expected arrival of the analysis
records.purpose: Gives the two lead-time figures the purchase analysis reports: how long an order took to be confirmed, and how far ahead of the deadline the goods were expected.

operands.name: confirmation date of the order
operands.source: the confirmation date field of the order
operands.constraints: an order without one contributes no delay

operands.name: order deadline
operands.source: the order deadline field
operands.constraints: the base of both differences

operands.name: expected arrival of the line
operands.source: the expected arrival field of the order line
operands.constraints: a line without one contributes no delay to expected arrival

preconditions.condition: The order carries a confirmation date.
preconditions.otherwise: The delay is not defined for that order and the figure is empty.

preconditions.condition: The line carries an expected arrival.
preconditions.otherwise: The delay to expected arrival is not defined for that line and the figure is empty.

procedure: Subtract the order deadline from the confirmation date and express the difference in days, giving the delay.
Subtract the order deadline from the line's expected arrival and express that difference in days, giving the delay to expected arrival.
Report both as signed numbers of days, so that a confirmation before the deadline gives a negative delay.
records.formula: delay = ( date_approve − date_order ) in days ; delay_pass = ( line.date_planned − date_order ) in days

rounding.what: The two figures as they are displayed.
rounding.precision: The number of decimal digits the report displays, which for a figure in days is two.
rounding.step: At display; the difference itself is computed at full precision.

result.name: delay and delay to expected arrival
result.unit_or_currency: days
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed by the purchase analysis report; not stored on the order.

edge_cases.case: The order was confirmed before its deadline.
edge_cases.outcome: The delay is negative.

edge_cases.case: The order was confirmed on the same day as its deadline but later in the day.
edge_cases.outcome: The delay is a positive fraction of a day, because the difference is a timestamp difference and not a date difference.

edge_cases.case: The line's expected arrival is earlier than the order deadline.
edge_cases.outcome: The delay to expected arrival is negative, which happens when the deadline was pushed forward after the line was created.

edge_cases.case: The order has no confirmation date.
edge_cases.outcome: The delay is empty and the row contributes none to a grouped average.

worked_examples.description: An order deadlined on the 1st, confirmed on the 3rd, whose line is expected on the 10th
worked_examples.narrative: The confirmation came two days after the deadline, so the delay is two days; the line was expected nine days after the deadline, so the delay to expected arrival is nine days.

records.name: The total and the untaxed total of the analysis
records.purpose: Gives the two money columns of the purchase analysis, each brought to the company currency by the order's own rate and then to the reader's presentation currency.

operands.name: total including tax of each line
operands.source: the computed line total
operands.constraints: summed over the rows of the group

operands.name: subtotal of each line
operands.source: the computed line subtotal
operands.constraints: summed over the rows of the group

operands.name: currency rate of each order
operands.source: the stored rate of the order the line belongs to
operands.constraints: strictly positive; each line is divided by its own order's rate

operands.name: presentation rate
operands.source: the currency table built for the reader's allowed companies
operands.constraints: applied after the rounding, not before

preconditions.condition: Each order carries a currency rate.
preconditions.otherwise: The rate is one and the amount passes through into the company currency unchanged.

preconditions.condition: A currency table has been built for the reader's allowed companies.
preconditions.otherwise: The presentation rate is one and the company-currency figure is shown as it stands.

procedure: Divide each line's total including tax by its own order's currency rate, bringing it into the company currency.
Sum those company-currency figures over the rows of the group.
Round the sum to two decimal digits.
Multiply the rounded sum by the presentation rate of the currency table built for the reader's allowed companies.
Repeat the same four steps on the line subtotals to obtain the untaxed total.
records.formula: price_total = round_to_precision( Σ ( line.price_total ÷ order.currency_rate ) , 2 ) × presentation_rate ; untaxed_total = round_to_precision( Σ ( line.price_subtotal ÷ order.currency_rate ) , 2 ) × presentation_rate

rounding.what: The summed company-currency amount, before the presentation rate is applied.
rounding.precision: Two decimal digits.
rounding.step: Once, after the sum and before the multiplication by the presentation rate, so that the presentation rate is applied to a rounded figure.

result.name: total and untaxed total of the analysis
result.unit_or_currency: the presentation currency of the reader's currency table
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed by the purchase analysis report; not stored.

edge_cases.case: Lines of several orders in several currencies.
edge_cases.outcome: Each line is divided by its own order's rate, so the sum is a proper company-currency figure and not a mixture.

edge_cases.case: The presentation rate is one.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure shown is the rounded company-currency sum.

edge_cases.case: The rounding is applied before the presentation rate.
edge_cases.outcome: A rebuild that multiplied first and rounded afterwards would produce a different last digit; the order of the two steps is part of the specification.

edge_cases.case: A line total is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: It lowers the sum by the same ratio.

worked_examples.description: Two lines in a foreign currency at an order rate of 1.25
worked_examples.narrative: Each line is divided by the order rate of 1.25, giving 96.80 and 193.60; the sum is 290.40, which is already exact at two digits, and the presentation rate of one leaves it at 290.40.

records.name: The average price of the analysis
records.purpose: Gives the price per reference unit of the product that the purchase analysis reports, weighting each line by its quantity rather than averaging the line prices.

operands.name: ordered quantity of each line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the total quantity field of the order line
operands.constraints: appears in both the numerator and the denominator

operands.name: unit price of each line
operands.unit_or_currency: the order currency per line unit
operands.source: the unit price field of the order line
operands.constraints: the numerator multiplies it by the quantity

operands.name: currency rate of each order
operands.source: the stored rate of the order the line belongs to
operands.constraints: strictly positive

operands.name: factor of the line unit and factor of the product reference unit
operands.source: the unit of measure records
operands.constraints: the denominator restates the quantities into the product reference unit

operands.name: presentation rate
operands.source: the currency table built for the reader's allowed companies
operands.constraints: applied after the rounding

preconditions.condition: The denominator is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The result is undefined and is returned as empty.

preconditions.condition: Each order carries a currency rate.
preconditions.otherwise: The rate is one and the amounts pass through unchanged.

procedure: For each line, multiply the ordered quantity by the unit price and divide by the order's currency rate; sum those figures into the numerator.

For each line, multiply the ordered quantity by the factor of the line unit and divide by the factor of the product reference unit; sum those figures into the denominator, which restates the quantities into the product reference unit.
Divide the numerator by the denominator, so that the average is a price per product reference unit rather than per line unit.
Round the quotient to two decimal digits and multiply by the presentation rate.
Return an empty figure when the denominator is zero.
records.formula: price_average = round_to_precision( Σ ( line.product_qty × line.price_unit ÷ order.currency_rate ) ÷ Σ ( line.product_qty × line_unit_factor ÷ product_unit_factor ) , 2 ) × presentation_rate , and empty when the denominator is zero

rounding.what: The quotient, before the presentation rate is applied.
rounding.precision: Two decimal digits.
rounding.step: Once, after the division and before the multiplication by the presentation rate.

result.name: average price per reference unit of the product
result.unit_or_currency: the presentation currency per reference unit of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed by the purchase analysis report; not stored.

edge_cases.case: Every line has a zero ordered quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The denominator is zero and the figure is empty rather than an error.

edge_cases.case: Lines bought in different units of the same category.
edge_cases.outcome: The denominator restates them all into the product reference unit, so the average is comparable across units.

edge_cases.case: Lines of several orders in several currencies.
edge_cases.outcome: Each numerator term is divided by its own order's rate before the sum.

edge_cases.case: A single line.
edge_cases.outcome: The average is that line's own unit price restated per product reference unit.

worked_examples.description: Ten boxes of twelve at 120.00 and twenty-four loose units at 10.50
worked_examples.narrative: The numerator is ten multiplied by 120.00 plus twenty-four multiplied by 10.50, that is 1 200.00 plus 252.00, or 1 452.00. The denominator restates the quantities into the product reference unit: ten boxes are one hundred and twenty units and the twenty-four loose units are twenty-four, giving one hundred and forty-four. The average is 1 452.00 divided by 144, that is 10.083333…, rounded to 10.08.

records.name: The ordered, received and billed quantities of the analysis
records.purpose: Gives the three quantity columns of the purchase analysis, all restated into the reference unit of the product so that lines bought in different units add up.

operands.name: ordered quantity of each line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the total quantity field of the order line
operands.constraints: restated into the product reference unit

operands.name: received quantity of each line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the computed received quantity
operands.constraints: restated into the product reference unit

operands.name: billed quantity of each line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the computed billed quantity
operands.constraints: restated into the product reference unit

operands.name: factor of the line unit and factor of the product reference unit
operands.source: the unit of measure records
operands.constraints: both strictly positive

preconditions.condition: The line unit and the product reference unit belong to the same category.
preconditions.otherwise: The restatement cannot be made; a line could not have been saved with a unit outside the product's category.

procedure: For each line, multiply the ordered quantity by the factor of the line unit and divide by the factor of the product reference unit; sum the results into the ordered column.
Do the same with the received quantity to obtain the received column.
Do the same with the billed quantity to obtain the billed column.
Report the three sums, all expressed in the reference unit of the product.
records.formula: qty_ordered = Σ ( line.product_qty × line_unit_factor ÷ product_unit_factor ) ; qty_received = Σ ( line.qty_received × line_unit_factor ÷ product_unit_factor ) ; qty_billed = Σ ( line.qty_invoiced × line_unit_factor ÷ product_unit_factor )

rounding.what: Each restated quantity as it is displayed.
rounding.precision: The Product Unit decimal precision.
rounding.step: At display; the restatement itself is not rounded before the sum.

result.name: ordered, received and billed quantities
result.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed by the purchase analysis report; not stored.

edge_cases.case: The line unit is the product reference unit.
edge_cases.outcome: The two factors are equal and the quantity passes through unchanged.

edge_cases.case: A line whose billed quantity exceeds its received quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The billed column exceeds the received column, which is what a bill received before the goods produces.

edge_cases.case: A refundable return.
edge_cases.outcome: The received column falls while the ordered column is unchanged.

edge_cases.case: A display line.
edge_cases.outcome: It carries no quantity and contributes nothing to any of the three columns.

worked_examples.description: Ten boxes of twelve, eight of them received and six billed
worked_examples.narrative: Ten boxes are one hundred and twenty units, eight boxes are ninety-six units and six boxes are seventy-two units.

records.name: The quantity still to be billed of the analysis under the ordered-quantities policy
records.purpose: Gives the analysis column that reports what remains to be billed for a product whose bill control policy is the ordered-quantities policy.

operands.name: ordered quantity of the analysis
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
operands.source: the restated ordered quantity column
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: billed quantity of the analysis
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
operands.source: the restated billed quantity column
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: bill control policy of the product
operands.source: the product setting, whose stored value for this policy is `purchase` (bill on ordered quantities)
operands.constraints: selects this variant

preconditions.condition: The product's bill control policy is the ordered-quantities policy.
preconditions.otherwise: The received-quantities variant applies instead.

procedure: Take the analysis ordered quantity, already restated into the product reference unit.
Subtract the analysis billed quantity, restated the same way.
Report the difference as the quantity still to be billed.
records.formula: qty_to_be_billed = qty_ordered − qty_billed , for a product whose bill control policy is `purchase`

rounding.what: The difference as it is displayed.
rounding.precision: The Product Unit decimal precision.
rounding.step: At display.

result.name: quantity still to be billed
result.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed by the purchase analysis report; not stored.

edge_cases.case: More has been billed than was ordered.
edge_cases.outcome: The column is negative.

edge_cases.case: Nothing has been billed.
edge_cases.outcome: The column equals the ordered quantity.

edge_cases.case: The order is not in the confirmed status.
edge_cases.outcome: The stored quantity to bill on the line is zero, but this analysis column is computed from the ordered and billed columns and can therefore differ from the line's own quantity to bill; the analysis reports the arithmetic difference.

edge_cases.case: A group of rows.
edge_cases.outcome: The two columns are summed first and the difference is taken over the sums.

worked_examples.description: One hundred and twenty units ordered and seventy-two billed
worked_examples.narrative: One hundred and twenty minus seventy-two leaves forty-eight units still to be billed.

records.name: The quantity still to be billed of the analysis under the received-quantities policy
records.purpose: Gives the analysis column that reports what remains to be billed for a product whose bill control policy is the received-quantities policy.

operands.name: received quantity of the analysis
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
operands.source: the restated received quantity column
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: billed quantity of the analysis
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
operands.source: the restated billed quantity column
operands.constraints: may be zero or negative

operands.name: bill control policy of the product
operands.source: the product setting, whose stored value for this policy is `receive` (bill on received quantities)
operands.constraints: selects this variant

preconditions.condition: The product's bill control policy is the received-quantities policy.
preconditions.otherwise: The ordered-quantities variant applies instead.

procedure: Take the analysis received quantity, already restated into the product reference unit.
Subtract the analysis billed quantity, restated the same way.
Report the difference as the quantity still to be billed.
records.formula: qty_to_be_billed = qty_received − qty_billed , for a product whose bill control policy is `receive`

rounding.what: The difference as it is displayed.
rounding.precision: The Product Unit decimal precision.
rounding.step: At display.

result.name: quantity still to be billed
result.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed by the purchase analysis report; not stored.

edge_cases.case: The vendor has billed more than has arrived.
edge_cases.outcome: The column is negative, which is what an over-billed line shows.

edge_cases.case: Nothing has arrived.
edge_cases.outcome: The column is minus the billed quantity.

edge_cases.case: A refundable return after everything was billed.
edge_cases.outcome: The received column falls and the column goes negative, which is the vendor refund that is due.

edge_cases.case: A group of rows.
edge_cases.outcome: The two columns are summed first and the difference is taken over the sums.

worked_examples.description: Ninety-six units received and seventy-two billed
worked_examples.narrative: Ninety-six minus seventy-two leaves twenty-four units still to be billed.

records.name: The weight and the volume of the analysis
records.purpose: Gives the two physical columns of the purchase analysis, each the product's own figure multiplied by the quantity restated into the product reference unit.

operands.name: weight of the product
operands.unit_or_currency: the weight unit configured for the system
operands.source: the product record
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: volume of the product
operands.unit_or_currency: the volume unit configured for the system
operands.source: the product record
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: ordered quantity of each line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the total quantity field of the order line
operands.constraints: restated into the product reference unit

operands.name: factor of the line unit and factor of the product reference unit
operands.source: the unit of measure records
operands.constraints: both strictly positive

preconditions.condition: The product carries a weight and a volume.
preconditions.otherwise: The missing figure is treated as zero and the column is zero for that line.

procedure: For each line, restate the ordered quantity into the product reference unit by multiplying by the factor of the line unit and dividing by the factor of the product reference unit.
Multiply the restated quantity by the product's weight and sum the results into the weight column.
Multiply the restated quantity by the product's volume and sum the results into the volume column.
records.formula: weight = Σ ( product.weight × line.product_qty × line_unit_factor ÷ product_unit_factor ) ; volume = Σ ( product.volume × line.product_qty × line_unit_factor ÷ product_unit_factor )

rounding.what: Each column as it is displayed.
rounding.precision: The number of decimal digits the report displays for a weight and for a volume.
rounding.step: At display; the products are summed at full precision.

result.name: total weight and total volume
result.unit_or_currency: the weight unit and the volume unit configured for the system
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed by the purchase analysis report; not stored.

edge_cases.case: The product has no weight.
edge_cases.outcome: Its contribution to the weight column is zero.

edge_cases.case: A service product.
edge_cases.outcome: Its weight and volume are zero and it contributes nothing.

edge_cases.case: Lines bought in different units.
edge_cases.outcome: Each quantity is restated into the product reference unit before it is multiplied, so the columns add up correctly.

edge_cases.case: A negative ordered quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The contribution is negative.

worked_examples.description: Ten boxes of twelve units of a product weighing two and a half each
worked_examples.narrative: Ten boxes are one hundred and twenty units; at 2.5 each the weight is 300.0 and at 0.01 each the volume is 1.2.

records.name: The days to arrival of the analysis
records.purpose: Gives how many days elapsed between the order deadline and the arrival of the goods, preferring the actual receipt date over the expected one.

operands.name: earliest completed receipt date of the line
operands.source: the completed goods movements of the order line
operands.constraints: used in preference to the expected arrival

operands.name: expected arrival of the line
operands.source: the expected arrival field of the order line
operands.constraints: used when no completed receipt exists

operands.name: order deadline
operands.source: the order deadline field
operands.constraints: the base of the difference

preconditions.condition: The line has either a completed receipt or an expected arrival.
preconditions.otherwise: The figure is empty for that line.

preconditions.condition: The order carries a deadline.
preconditions.otherwise: No difference can be formed and the figure is empty.

procedure: Take the earliest completed receipt date of the line, or, when the line has none, its expected arrival.
Subtract the order deadline from that timestamp.
Express the difference in days and report it.
records.formula: days_to_arrival = ( earliest completed receipt date , or line.date_planned ) − date_order , in days

rounding.what: The figure as it is displayed.
rounding.precision: The number of decimal digits the report displays for a figure in days, which is two.
rounding.step: At display; the difference is computed at full precision.

result.name: days to arrival
result.unit_or_currency: days
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed by the purchase analysis report; not stored.

edge_cases.case: The goods have arrived.
edge_cases.outcome: The actual receipt date is used, so the figure reports the real lead time rather than the planned one.

edge_cases.case: The goods have not arrived.
edge_cases.outcome: The expected arrival is used, so the figure reports the planned lead time.

edge_cases.case: The goods arrived before the order deadline.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure is negative, which happens when the deadline was pushed forward after the receipt.

edge_cases.case: Several completed receipts exist for the line.
edge_cases.outcome: The earliest is used.

worked_examples.description: An order deadlined on the 21st whose goods arrived on the 28th
worked_examples.narrative: The actual receipt date of the 28th is preferred over the expected arrival of the 30th, so the figure is seven days rather than nine.

records.name: The re-aggregated average price
records.purpose: Replaces the plain average of row averages by a quantity-weighted average when rows of the purchase analysis are grouped, so that a large line is not weighted like a small one.

operands.name: average price of each row
operands.unit_or_currency: the presentation currency per reference unit of the product
operands.source: the computed average price of the row
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: ordered quantity of each row
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product
operands.source: the restated ordered quantity of the row
operands.constraints: the weight of that row

preconditions.condition: The summed ordered quantity of the group is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing is returned; the grouped average is empty rather than zero or an error.

procedure: Multiply each row's average price by that row's ordered quantity.
Sum those products over the rows of the group.
Sum the ordered quantities over the rows of the group.
Divide the first sum by the second; return nothing when the second sum is zero.
records.formula: grouped_price_average = Σ ( row.price_average × row.qty_ordered ) ÷ Σ row.qty_ordered , and nothing when the denominator is zero

rounding.what: The grouped average as it is displayed.
rounding.precision: Two decimal digits.
rounding.step: At display; the weighted sum and the division are carried at full precision.

result.name: grouped average price
result.unit_or_currency: the presentation currency per reference unit of the product
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed by the purchase analysis report for the group; not stored.

edge_cases.case: Every row has a zero ordered quantity.
edge_cases.outcome: The denominator is zero and the grouped average is empty.

edge_cases.case: A single row in the group.
edge_cases.outcome: The weighted average equals that row's own average.

edge_cases.case: One row is far larger than the others.
edge_cases.outcome: It dominates the grouped average, which is the intended behaviour and is why a plain average of the row averages is not used.

edge_cases.case: A row with a zero average price.
edge_cases.outcome: It contributes nothing to the numerator but still contributes its quantity to the denominator, so it pulls the grouped average down.

worked_examples.description: Two rows of very different sizes
worked_examples.narrative: The weighted numerator is one hundred multiplied by 10.00 plus five multiplied by 30.00, that is 1 150; the denominator is one hundred and five; and 1 150 divided by 105 is 10.95. A plain average of the two row averages would have given 20.00 and would have been wrong.

records.name: The late-order search predicate
records.purpose: Gives the stored search that finds late orders, and the inversion that finds the ones that are not late, so that the same records are selected by a rebuild.

operands.name: status of the order
operands.source: the status field of the order, whose confirmed value is `purchase`
operands.constraints: only a confirmed order can be late

operands.name: expected arrival of the order
operands.source: the header expected arrival
operands.constraints: compared with the current moment

operands.name: status of each transfer of the order
operands.source: the transfers linked to the order, when inventory is installed
operands.constraints: an order every one of whose transfers is completed or cancelled is not late

operands.name: received quantity and ordered quantity of each line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the order lines
operands.constraints: compared at the rounding of the line unit

operands.name: operator used in the search
operands.source: the search being built
operands.constraints: only equality and inequality are accepted

preconditions.condition: The operator used is equality or inequality.
preconditions.otherwise: The search is refused with "Unsupported operator".

preconditions.condition: Inventory is installed.
preconditions.otherwise: The transfer clause is omitted and the order part is the status and the arrival test alone.

procedure: Build the order part: the status is the confirmed status, the expected arrival is on or before the current moment, and, when inventory is installed, either no transfer exists or at least one transfer is neither completed nor cancelled.
Build the line part: the received quantity is strictly below the ordered quantity.

Combine the two with a logical and, so that the order is selected when it has at least one line whose order satisfies the order part and whose received quantity is strictly below its ordered quantity.
For the not-late search, invert the line part to a received quantity that is greater than or equal to the ordered quantity, while keeping the order part unchanged.
Refuse any other operator with the message "Unsupported operator".
records.formula: order_part = ( state = `purchase` ) and ( date_planned ≤ now ) and ( no transfer exists or some transfer's state ∉ { completed , cancelled } ) when inventory is installed ; line_part = ( qty_received < product_qty ) for the late search , and ( qty_received ≥ product_qty ) for the not-late search ; the order is selected when order_part and line_part both hold on at least one line

rounding.what: The two quantities of the line part.
rounding.precision: The rounding of the line's unit of measure.
rounding.step: At the comparison of the received quantity with the ordered quantity.

result.name: the set of orders the search returns
result.unit_or_currency: not applicable
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; the search is a stored filter of the order list.

edge_cases.case: An order whose transfers are all completed.
edge_cases.outcome: The order part fails and the order is not late, however short the receipts were.

edge_cases.case: An order with no transfer at all, for example one of services only.
edge_cases.outcome: The transfer clause accepts it, so the order can still be late on the line part.

edge_cases.case: An order whose expected arrival is exactly the current moment.
edge_cases.outcome: The test is on or before, so it counts as due and the order can be late.

edge_cases.case: The not-late search.
edge_cases.outcome: The order part is unchanged and only the line part is inverted, so an order that is not confirmed is in neither result set.

edge_cases.case: An unsupported operator is used.
edge_cases.outcome: The search is refused with "Unsupported operator".

worked_examples.description: A confirmed order due yesterday with one line short

inputs.transfers: one transfer that is neither completed nor cancelled

worked_examples.narrative: The order is confirmed, its expected arrival has passed and its transfer is open, so the order part holds; six received is strictly below ten ordered, so the line part holds and the order is late. The not-late search inverts only the line part, which then fails, so the order is not returned by it.

records.name: Purchased quantity of a product variant over the last year
records.purpose: Gives how much of a product variant has been bought in the last year, which is shown on the product and used to judge purchasing volume.

operands.name: total quantity of each qualifying line
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the lines of confirmed orders whose confirmation date is on or after today minus one year
operands.constraints: summed and then rounded to the product reference unit

operands.name: confirmation date of each order
operands.source: the order holding the line
operands.constraints: must be on or after today minus one year

operands.name: reference unit of measure of the product variant
operands.source: the product variant
operands.constraints: the rounding target of the sum

preconditions.condition: The order is confirmed and carries a confirmation date.
preconditions.otherwise: Its lines are not counted.

preconditions.condition: The confirmation date is on or after today minus one year.
preconditions.otherwise: The line is not counted.

procedure: Select the purchase order lines of the variant whose order is confirmed and whose confirmation date is on or after today minus one year.
Sum their total quantities.
Round the sum to the rounding of the product variant's reference unit.
records.formula: purchased_product_qty( variant ) = round_to_unit( Σ over the lines of confirmed orders whose confirmation date ≥ today − 1 year of line.total_quantity , product_reference_unit )

rounding.what: The summed quantity.
rounding.precision: The rounding of the product variant's reference unit.
rounding.step: Once, after the sum.

result.name: purchased quantity of the variant over the last year
result.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the product variant
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the product variant; recomputed rather than stored permanently.

edge_cases.case: No order of the variant was confirmed in the last year.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure is zero.

edge_cases.case: An order confirmed exactly one year ago today.
edge_cases.outcome: It is counted, because the test is on or after today minus one year.

edge_cases.case: An order that was reset to draft after confirmation.
edge_cases.outcome: Its confirmation date is not cleared by the reset, but the order is no longer confirmed, so its lines are not counted.

edge_cases.case: Lines expressed in different units.
edge_cases.outcome: The sum is rounded to the product reference unit, so the figure is comparable across lines.

worked_examples.description: Three confirmed lines within the year
worked_examples.narrative: The three lines add to 200.0, which is already a whole number of reference units, so the figure is 200.

records.name: Purchased quantity of a product template over the last year
records.purpose: Gives the same figure at the template level, summed over the template's variants including the archived ones.

operands.name: purchased quantity of each variant of the template
operands.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the variant
operands.source: the computed purchased quantity of each variant
operands.constraints: archived variants are included

operands.name: reference unit of measure of the template
operands.source: the product template
operands.constraints: the rounding target of the sum

preconditions.condition: The template has at least one variant.
preconditions.otherwise: The figure is zero.

preconditions.condition: The archived variants are included in the sum.
preconditions.otherwise: A template whose older variants have been archived would understate its purchasing volume.

procedure: Compute the purchased quantity of each variant of the template over the last year, including the archived variants.
Sum those figures.
Round the sum to the rounding of the template's reference unit.
records.formula: purchased_product_qty( template ) = round_to_unit( Σ over its variants of purchased_product_qty( variant ) , template_reference_unit )

rounding.what: The summed quantity.
rounding.precision: The rounding of the template's reference unit.
rounding.step: Once, after the sum; each variant figure was already rounded to its own reference unit.

result.name: purchased quantity of the template over the last year
result.unit_or_currency: the reference unit of the template
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the product template; recomputed rather than stored permanently.

edge_cases.case: Every variant is archived.
edge_cases.outcome: They are still included and the template figure is the sum of their purchased quantities.

edge_cases.case: The template has one variant only.
edge_cases.outcome: The template figure equals the variant figure.

edge_cases.case: Two roundings apply, one per variant and one on the template sum.
edge_cases.outcome: The template figure can differ in the last digit from a single rounding of the raw line quantities; the two-step rounding is part of the specification.

worked_examples.description: A template of two variants, one of them archived
worked_examples.narrative: The active variant contributes 200 and the archived one 45, so the template figure is 245.

records.name: The analytic contribution of a purchase order line to a project
records.purpose: Gives the fraction of a purchase order line that belongs to a project's analytic account, and the money that fraction represents.

operands.name: percentages of the line's analytic distribution
operands.source: the analytic distribution of the purchase order line, keyed by combinations of analytic accounts
operands.constraints: the percentages of the keys that mention the project's analytic account are summed

operands.name: analytic account of the project
operands.source: the project
operands.constraints: the account whose keys are counted

operands.name: subtotal of the line
operands.source: the computed line subtotal
operands.constraints: converted into the project's currency

operands.name: currency of the project
operands.source: the project
operands.constraints: the target of the conversion

operands.name: status of the order
operands.source: the order holding the line
operands.constraints: only a confirmed order contributes

preconditions.condition: The order is confirmed.
preconditions.otherwise: The line contributes nothing to the project's figures.

preconditions.condition: The line's analytic distribution mentions the project's analytic account.
preconditions.otherwise: The contribution is zero and the line is not selected at all.

procedure: Sum the percentages of every distribution key that mentions the project's analytic account.
Divide that sum by one hundred, giving the line's analytic contribution as a fraction.
Convert the line's subtotal into the project's currency.
Multiply the converted subtotal by the contribution fraction, giving the line's amount attributable to the project.
records.formula: analytic_contribution( line ) = ( Σ over the distribution keys that mention the project's analytic account of percentage ) ÷ 100 ; line_amount_to_invoice = convert( line.price_subtotal , to = project_currency ) × analytic_contribution( line )

rounding.what: The converted subtotal.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the project's currency.
rounding.step: At the currency conversion; the contribution fraction is not rounded.

result.name: analytic contribution fraction and the line's amount attributable to the project
result.unit_or_currency: a fraction, and the project's currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the project profitability figures.

edge_cases.case: Several distribution keys mention the same analytic account.
edge_cases.outcome: Their percentages are added, so a line split across two combinations that both mention the account contributes the sum of the two.

edge_cases.case: The distribution mentions the account at one hundred per cent.
edge_cases.outcome: The whole line subtotal is attributable to the project.

edge_cases.case: The order is not confirmed.
edge_cases.outcome: The line is not selected and contributes nothing.

edge_cases.case: The project's currency differs from the order currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The subtotal is converted before the fraction is applied.

worked_examples.description: A line of one thousand split sixty per cent to the project
worked_examples.narrative: Sixty divided by one hundred is a contribution of 0.6, and one thousand multiplied by 0.6 is 600.00 attributable to the project.

records.name: The cost of a bill line attributed to a project
records.purpose: Gives the money a single vendor bill line costs a project, with the refund sign applied, which the project's billed and still-to-bill figures both consume.

operands.name: subtotal of the bill line
operands.source: the bill line linked to the purchase order line
operands.constraints: converted into the project's currency

operands.name: analytic contribution of the bill line
operands.source: the sum of the percentages of the bill line's distribution keys that mention the project's analytic account, divided by one hundred
operands.constraints: between zero and one in ordinary use

operands.name: document type of the bill line's document
operands.source: the document holding the bill line
operands.constraints: a vendor refund gives a sign of minus one and anything else plus one

operands.name: currency of the project
operands.source: the project
operands.constraints: the target of the conversion

preconditions.condition: The bill line's document is not cancelled.
preconditions.otherwise: The bill line is not counted at all.

preconditions.condition: The bill line's distribution mentions the project's analytic account.
preconditions.otherwise: The contribution is zero and the cost is zero.

procedure: Convert the bill line's subtotal into the project's currency.
Sum the percentages of the bill line's distribution keys that mention the project's analytic account and divide by one hundred, giving the contribution fraction.
Multiply the converted subtotal by the contribution fraction.
Multiply by minus one when the bill line belongs to a vendor refund, and by plus one otherwise.
records.formula: cost( bill_line ) = convert( bill_line.price_subtotal , to = project_currency ) × analytic_contribution( bill_line ) × ( −1 when the bill line belongs to a vendor refund , +1 otherwise )

rounding.what: The converted subtotal.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the project's currency.
rounding.step: At the currency conversion; the contribution fraction and the sign are not rounded.

result.name: cost of the bill line attributable to the project
result.unit_or_currency: the project's currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; accumulated into the project's billed amount and its amount still to bill.

edge_cases.case: The bill line belongs to a vendor refund.
edge_cases.outcome: The sign is minus one and the cost is negative, which reverses the project's billed amount by that much.

edge_cases.case: The bill line's document is cancelled.
edge_cases.outcome: The line is excluded altogether.

edge_cases.case: The bill line's distribution differs from the order line's.
edge_cases.outcome: The bill line's own distribution governs its cost, not the order line's.

edge_cases.case: The bill is in a different currency from the project.
edge_cases.outcome: The subtotal is converted before the fraction is applied.

worked_examples.description: A posted bill line of four hundred split sixty per cent to the project
worked_examples.narrative: Four hundred multiplied by the contribution of 0.6 is 240.00, and the sign is plus one because the document is a vendor bill.

records.name: The accumulation into the project's billed amount and amount still to bill
records.purpose: Gives how the purchase order lines and their bill lines add up into the two project profitability figures, and why both are negative.

operands.name: cost of each posted bill line
operands.source: the computed cost of the bill line
operands.constraints: subtracted from the billed amount

operands.name: cost of each draft bill line
operands.source: the computed cost of the bill line
operands.constraints: subtracted from the amount still to bill

operands.name: amount attributable to the project of each purchase order line
operands.source: the computed line amount
operands.constraints: the base of the last term

operands.name: cost of each non-refund bill line of that purchase line
operands.source: the computed cost of the bill line
operands.constraints: summed and deducted from the last term

preconditions.condition: The purchase order is confirmed.
preconditions.otherwise: Neither its line nor its bill lines contribute.

preconditions.condition: The bill line is not cancelled and mentions the project's analytic account.
preconditions.otherwise: It is excluded from every accumulation.

procedure: For every posted bill line of the selected purchase lines, subtract its cost from the project's billed amount.
For every draft bill line of those purchase lines, subtract its cost from the project's amount still to bill.

For every purchase line, subtract from the amount still to bill the line's amount attributable to the project less the sum of the costs of its non-refund bill lines, so that what has already been billed is not counted twice.
Apply only the last term when a purchase line has no bill line at all.
Keep both figures negative, because purchases are costs.
records.formula: amount_invoiced = amount_invoiced − cost( bill_line ) for every posted bill line ; amount_to_invoice = amount_to_invoice − cost( bill_line ) for every draft bill line ; amount_to_invoice = amount_to_invoice − ( line_amount_to_invoice − Σ cost( bill_line ) over the non-refund bill lines )

rounding.what: Each accumulated figure as it is written.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the project's currency.
rounding.step: When each figure is written; the individual costs were rounded at their own currency conversion.

result.name: project billed amount and project amount still to bill
result.unit_or_currency: the project's currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the project's profitability panel; not stored on the purchase records.

edge_cases.case: A purchase line with no bill line at all.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the last term applies and the whole attributable amount lands in the amount still to bill.

edge_cases.case: A purchase line fully billed by posted bills.
edge_cases.outcome: The last term is the attributable amount less the costs of the non-refund bill lines, which is zero, so the amount still to bill is unchanged and the whole cost sits in the billed amount.

edge_cases.case: A refund bill line.
edge_cases.outcome: Its cost is negative, so it raises the billed amount towards zero; it is also excluded from the deduction in the last term, which is why the term names the non-refund bill lines only.

edge_cases.case: A draft bill line.
edge_cases.outcome: Its cost lowers the amount still to bill, so a bill prepared but not yet posted is already reflected in the figure still expected.

worked_examples.description: A line of one thousand split sixty per cent, partly billed
worked_examples.narrative: The purchase line contributes minus 600.00 to the amount still to bill. A posted bill line of four hundred split sixty per cent contributes 240.00 of cost, which lowers the billed amount to minus 240.00 and reduces the amount still to bill by the same 240.00, leaving minus 360.00 still to bill.

records.name: The per-line accrued-expense amount
records.purpose: Gives the amount each selected purchase order line contributes to an accrued-expense entry, which recognises goods and services received but not yet billed at a period end.

operands.name: quantity still to bill at the accrual date
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the at-date quantity computed under the product's bill control policy
operands.constraints: a line whose figure is zero at the line unit's rounding is not selected

operands.name: unit price used for the line
operands.unit_or_currency: the order currency per line unit
operands.source: the line's discounted unit price, or the price recomputed from the posted bills when the vendor has over-billed
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: taxes of the line
operands.source: the tax set of the order line
operands.constraints: when any tax is included in the price, the tax engine is asked for the amount excluding tax instead

operands.name: order currency and company currency
operands.source: the order and its company
operands.constraints: the amount is rounded in the order currency and then converted

preconditions.condition: The line is not a display line and is not a down payment.
preconditions.otherwise: It is excluded from the accrual selection.

preconditions.condition: The line belongs to one of the selected orders and its amount still to bill at the chosen date is not zero at the line unit's rounding.
preconditions.otherwise: It is excluded from the accrual selection.

preconditions.condition: Every selected order shares one currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The entry is refused with "Cannot create an accrual entry with orders in different currencies."

preconditions.condition: Every selected order belongs to one company.
preconditions.otherwise: The entry is refused with "Entries can only be created for a single company at a time."

procedure: Start from the line's discounted unit price.

Compute the over-billed quantity as the billed quantity at the accrual date minus the received quantity at the accrual date; when it is one or more, replace the unit price by the figure recomputed from the posted bills.
Multiply the quantity still to bill at the accrual date by the unit price, giving the subtotal.
When any of the line's taxes is included in the price, ask the tax engine instead for the amount excluding tax at that price and quantity.
Round the subtotal to the order currency and then convert it into the company currency.
records.formula: price_subtotal = qty_to_invoice_at_date × price_unit , except that the tax engine supplies the amount excluding tax when any of the line's taxes is included in the price ; the result is rounded to the order currency and then converted to the company currency

rounding.what: The per-line subtotal.
