rounding.precision: The rounding step of the order currency, and then of the company currency after the conversion.
rounding.step: Once in the order currency, before the conversion into the company currency; the conversion itself is the ordinary rounded conversion.

result.name: per-line accrued amount
result.unit_or_currency: the order currency, then the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Written as the amount of one journal item of the accrued-expense entry, debited when positive and credited when negative.

edge_cases.case: The quantity still to bill at the date is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The amount is negative, the expense account is credited and the accrual account debited, deferring the over-billed expense to the next period.

edge_cases.case: A tax of the line is included in the price.
edge_cases.outcome: The tax engine supplies the amount excluding tax, so the accrual recognises the net expense and not the tax.

edge_cases.case: Exactly one order is selected and its currency differs from the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: Each item also stores the order-currency amount and the order currency.

edge_cases.case: An amount is supplied on the assistant and exactly one order is selected.
edge_cases.outcome: The whole entry is that single manual amount instead of a per-line computation.

edge_cases.case: The product's category defines both an expense account and a stock-variation account for perpetual valuation.
edge_cases.outcome: The stock-variation account is used instead of the expense account; otherwise the expense account resolved from the product's template with the order's fiscal position applied is used.

worked_examples.description: Six of ten units received and none billed, at one hundred each
worked_examples.narrative: The amount still to bill at the date is six minus zero, that is six units, at 100.00 each, so the per-line amount is 600.00. The expense account is debited 600.00 and the accrual account credited 600.00; the reversal on the following day mirrors both.

records.name: The unit price recomputed when the vendor has over-billed
records.purpose: Replaces the line's discounted unit price by a price derived from the posted bills when more has been billed than has arrived, so that the accrual reverses what was actually charged.

operands.name: billed quantity at the accrual date
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the billed quantity recomputed over the bill lines dated on or before the accrual date
operands.constraints: the first term of the over-billed quantity

operands.name: received quantity at the accrual date
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the received quantity recomputed over the completed movements dated on or before the accrual date
operands.constraints: the second term of the over-billed quantity

operands.name: subtotals of the posted bill lines dated on or before the accrual date
operands.source: the posted bills of the line
operands.constraints: summed into the value already billed

operands.name: discounted unit price of the line
operands.unit_or_currency: the order currency per line unit
operands.source: the line's unit price after its discount
operands.constraints: used to value what has been received

preconditions.condition: The over-billed quantity is one or more.
preconditions.otherwise: The line's discounted unit price is kept and no recomputation is made.

preconditions.condition: The over-billed quantity is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The division is undefined; a value of one or more is required for the branch to be taken at all.

procedure: Compute the over-billed quantity as the billed quantity at the accrual date minus the received quantity at the accrual date.
When it is below one, keep the discounted unit price and stop.
Otherwise sum the subtotals of the posted bill lines dated on or before the accrual date.
Subtract from that sum the received quantity at the date multiplied by the discounted unit price, giving the value still to invoice.
Divide the value still to invoice by the over-billed quantity, giving the recomputed unit price.
records.formula: value_to_invoice = Σ ( the subtotals of the posted bill lines dated on or before the accrual date ) − ( received_at_date × discounted_unit_price ) ; price_unit = value_to_invoice ÷ over_billed_quantity , where over_billed_quantity = billed_at_date − received_at_date

rounding.what: The recomputed unit price, when the per-line subtotal that uses it is rounded.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the order currency, applied to the subtotal rather than to the price.
rounding.step: At the per-line subtotal, not at the price itself, which is carried at full precision.

result.name: recomputed unit price of the line
result.unit_or_currency: the order currency per line unit
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; used in place of the discounted unit price when the per-line accrued amount is computed.

edge_cases.case: The over-billed quantity is exactly one.
edge_cases.outcome: The branch is taken, because the test is one or more.

edge_cases.case: Nothing has been received.
edge_cases.outcome: The value still to invoice is the whole sum of the posted bill subtotals and the recomputed price is that sum divided by the billed quantity.

edge_cases.case: The posted bills exactly match the received value.
edge_cases.outcome: The value still to invoice is zero and the recomputed price is zero, so the accrual amount is zero.

edge_cases.case: The vendor has billed less than has arrived.
edge_cases.outcome: The over-billed quantity is negative, the branch is not taken and the discounted unit price is kept.

worked_examples.description: Eight units billed against six received at one hundred each
worked_examples.narrative: The over-billed quantity is eight minus six, that is two, which is at least one, so the price is recomputed: the posted bill subtotals of 800.00 less the received value of six multiplied by 100.00, that is 600.00, leaves a value to invoice of 200.00, and dividing by two gives a recomputed price of 100.00. The quantity still to bill at the date is six minus eight, that is minus two, so the per-line amount is minus 200.00: the expense account is credited 200.00 and the accrual account debited 200.00.

records.name: The price-difference addendum of the accrual entry
records.purpose: Adds two further journal items per line when the product resolves a price-difference account, so that the accrual also carries the gap between the standard cost and the price actually charged.

operands.name: standard cost of the product
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency per reference unit
operands.source: the cost field of the product
operands.constraints: may be zero

operands.name: unit price used for the line
operands.unit_or_currency: the order currency per line unit
operands.source: the discounted unit price, or the price recomputed when the vendor has over-billed
operands.constraints: the same price the per-line amount used

operands.name: received quantity at the accrual date
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the restricted received quantity
operands.constraints: the first term of the quantity difference

operands.name: billed quantity at the accrual date
operands.unit_or_currency: the unit of measure of the line
operands.source: the restricted billed quantity
operands.constraints: the second term of the quantity difference

operands.name: price-difference account of the product and stock-variation account of its category
operands.source: the product and its category
operands.constraints: both must resolve for the two items to be appended

preconditions.condition: The product resolves a price-difference account.
preconditions.otherwise: No addendum is appended and the accrual entry carries only its per-line items and its balancing item.

preconditions.condition: The price difference is not zero at the order currency's rounding.
preconditions.otherwise: No addendum is appended for that line.

procedure: Subtract the unit price used for the line from the product's standard cost, giving the price difference per unit.
Subtract the billed quantity at the accrual date from the received quantity at the accrual date, giving the quantity difference.
Multiply the two, giving the price difference.

When the price difference is not zero at the order currency's rounding, append two items: the product's price-difference account for minus the price difference, and the category's stock-variation account for plus the price difference.
Give neither item an analytic distribution.
records.formula: unit_price_diff = product.standard_price − price_unit ; price_diff = ( received_at_date − billed_at_date ) × unit_price_diff ; the price-difference account takes − price_diff and the stock-variation account takes + price_diff

rounding.what: The price difference, when it is compared with zero and when the two items are written.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the order currency for the zero test, and of the company currency for the item amounts.
rounding.step: At the zero test and again when each item amount is written.

result.name: the two addendum journal items
result.unit_or_currency: the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Appended to the accrued-expense entry, both without an analytic distribution.

edge_cases.case: The standard cost equals the price used.
edge_cases.outcome: The price difference per unit is zero, the price difference is zero, and no addendum is appended.

edge_cases.case: The vendor has over-billed.
edge_cases.outcome: The quantity difference is negative and the two items swap sides.

edge_cases.case: The product resolves no price-difference account.
edge_cases.outcome: No addendum is appended at all.

edge_cases.case: The category resolves no stock-variation account.
edge_cases.outcome: The pair cannot be balanced and the addendum is not appended.

worked_examples.description: Six units received and none billed, a standard cost of ninety against a price of one hundred
worked_examples.narrative: The difference per unit is 90.00 minus 100.00, that is minus 10.00, and the quantity difference is six, so the price difference is minus 60.00. The price-difference account therefore takes plus 60.00 and the stock-variation account minus 60.00, and neither item carries an analytic distribution.

records.name: The weighted analytic blend of the balancing accrual item
records.purpose: Gives the analytic distribution the single balancing item of an accrued-expense entry carries, which is a blend of the selected lines' distributions weighted by their totals.

operands.name: analytic distribution of each selected line
operands.source: the purchase order lines selected for the entry
operands.constraints: a line without a distribution contributes nothing to the blend

operands.name: total including tax of each selected line
operands.source: the computed line total
operands.constraints: the weight of that line

operands.name: sum of the selected orders' totals
operands.source: the totals of the orders the lines belong to
operands.constraints: the divisor of every weight

operands.name: per-line accrued amounts
operands.source: the computed per-line amounts
operands.constraints: their total, negated, is the balancing item's amount

preconditions.condition: At least one selected order carries a total that is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: No weight can be formed and the balancing item carries no analytic distribution.

preconditions.condition: The lines carry analytic distributions.
preconditions.otherwise: The balancing item carries none.

procedure: For each selected line, divide its total including tax by the sum of the selected orders' totals, giving that line's weight.
Multiply each percentage of that line's analytic distribution by the line's weight.
Accumulate the weighted percentages per analytic account across every selected line, giving the blend.
Give the balancing item that blend, and give each per-line item its own line's distribution unchanged.
Set the balancing item's amount to minus the total of the per-line amounts, on the opposite side, with the label "Accrued total".
records.formula: weight( line ) = line.price_total ÷ Σ ( the selected orders' totals ) ; blended percentage per analytic account = Σ over the lines of ( the line's percentage for that account × weight( line ) ) ; balancing item amount = − Σ ( the per-line amounts )

rounding.what: The blended percentages and the balancing amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency for the amount; the percentages keep the precision of the distribution.
rounding.step: When the balancing item is written; the weights themselves are not rounded.

result.name: analytic distribution and amount of the balancing item
result.unit_or_currency: percentages per analytic account, and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the single balancing journal item of the accrued-expense entry, posted to the chosen accrual account.

edge_cases.case: Every selected line shares one analytic distribution.
edge_cases.outcome: The weights add to one and the blend equals that distribution.

edge_cases.case: One line carries no distribution.
edge_cases.outcome: It contributes nothing to the blend but still contributes its weight to the divisor, so the blended percentages fall short of one hundred.

edge_cases.case: The selected orders' totals sum to zero.
edge_cases.outcome: No weight can be formed and the balancing item carries no analytic distribution.

edge_cases.case: Exactly one order is selected and its currency differs from the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: Each item, the balancing one included, also stores the order-currency amount and the order currency.

worked_examples.description: Two lines weighted by their totals
worked_examples.narrative: The first line weighs 600 divided by 1 000, that is 0.6, and the second 0.4, so the blend gives account A sixty per cent and account B forty per cent. The balancing item's amount is minus the total of the two per-line amounts, that is minus 1 000.00, posted to the accrual account on the opposite side under the label "Accrued total".

records.name: The accrual date and its reversal date
records.purpose: Gives the two dates an accrued-expense entry defaults to and the constraint between them, since both decide which period the expense falls in.

operands.name: first day of the current month
operands.source: the current date
operands.constraints: the base of the default accrual date

operands.name: accrual date chosen by the accountant
operands.source: the accrued-expense assistant
operands.constraints: required; defaulted to the last day of the previous month

operands.name: reversal date chosen by the accountant
operands.source: the accrued-expense assistant
operands.constraints: required; defaulted to the accrual date plus one day and overridable

preconditions.condition: The reversal date is strictly after the accrual date.
preconditions.otherwise: The entry is refused with "Reversal date must be posterior to date."

preconditions.condition: Both dates are supplied.
preconditions.otherwise: Both are required, so the assistant cannot proceed without them.

procedure: Default the accrual date to the first day of the current month minus one day, that is the last day of the previous month.
Default the reversal date to the accrual date plus one day.
Allow the accountant to override either date.
Refuse the entry unless the reversal date is strictly after the accrual date.

Post the entry at the accrual date and its reversing entry at the reversal date, the reversing entry carrying the reference "Reversal of: the original reference" and the name `/` so that the journal's own numbering applies on posting.
records.formula: default accrual date = first day of the current month − 1 day ; default reversal date = accrual date + 1 day ; the entry is refused unless reversal date > accrual date

rounding.what: Nothing: both are calendar dates.
rounding.precision: Not applicable.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: accrual date and reversal date of the entry
result.unit_or_currency: calendar dates
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the accrued-expense entry and on its reversing entry.

edge_cases.case: The current month is January.
edge_cases.outcome: The first day of the current month minus one day is the last day of December of the previous year, so the default accrual date crosses the year end.

edge_cases.case: The accountant sets the reversal date equal to the accrual date.
edge_cases.outcome: The entry is refused with "Reversal date must be posterior to date."

edge_cases.case: The accountant sets a reversal date several days later.
edge_cases.outcome: It is accepted; only the strict ordering is enforced.

edge_cases.case: The entry is posted.
edge_cases.outcome: A reversing entry is created and posted too, and every order that received an entry gets a message in its thread reading "Accrual entry created on the date: the entry link. And its reverse entry: the reverse entry link.", where the date is the accrual date and the two links point at the two entries.

worked_examples.description: An entry defaulted at the end of a thirty-one-day month
worked_examples.narrative: The first day of the current month minus one day is the 31st of the previous month, and the reversal date defaults to one day later, the 1st of the current month.
